544886|2026-06.headline: Tempsens Q1 FY27 revenue rose 33% to INR118 crores, but EBITDA margin fell to 22% from 25.3% on higher employee cost.
544886|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations grew 33% YoY to INR118 crores, led by Electrical Heating (+148.8% to INR25 crores) and Temperature Sensing (+42% to INR60 crores), while Specialized Cables fell 8.8% to INR32.5 crores on export order timing. EBITDA rose 15.7% to INR26.6 crores, but margin compressed about 330 bps to 22%, driven by a roughly 140 bps hit from employee cost (up 45% to INR20.4 crores) and a high prior-year gross margin base. Management guided FY27 revenue growth in line with the three-year blended growth rate and said margins should recover in H2 FY27. Four capacity projects with aggregate peak revenue potential of about INR500 crores are slated to commission between Q4 FY27 and Q3 FY28.

segments.name: Temperature Sensing
segments.commentary: Revenue INR60 crores, up 42%, led by thermal power and OEMs including CVD equipment makers; EDGE pyrometer series (with Micro-Epsilon) to start dispatch in Q3 FY27.

segments.name: Electrical Heating
segments.commentary: Revenue INR25 crores, up 148.8% on oil and gas dispatches in India, Southeast Asia and Middle East; 5-year standard furnace supply contract signed with a life sciences OEM.

segments.name: Specialized Cables
segments.commentary: Revenue INR32.5 crores, down 8.8% on export order timing; cable harness line launched with UL certification; Unit 8 greenfield under construction, completion by Q2 FY28.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth expected in line with blended three-year growth; management pointed to about 25% in analyst's framing but said visibility improves in H2.
EBITDA margin to remain broadly similar to FY26 profile; margin recovery visible in H2 FY27 as employee cost is absorbed by revenue.
Management expects profit growth to be in line with revenue growth by end of FY27.
Lower finance cost to be visible from the coming quarter after INR55 crores of IPO proceeds used for debt repayment.
OEM and new products expected to contribute more than 25% of revenue starting FY28.
capex_capacity: Brownfield 50,000 sq ft plant in Unit 1 for OEM contact sensors, commissioning by Q3 FY28, peak revenue potential about INR120 crores.

50,000 sq ft plant in Unit 6 for medium-voltage heaters, completion by Q1 FY28, peak revenue potential about INR200 crores; heaters tested to 7.2 kV, explosion-proof certification targeted by Q4 FY27.
Unit 8 greenfield cable plant, completion by Q2 FY28, peak revenue potential about INR60 crores; capacity can be ramped quickly.
Victura JV to acquire 80,000 sq ft facility with existing shed; production to start by Q4 FY27, peak revenue potential about INR120 crores.

Aggregate peak revenue potential of about INR500 crores across four projects versus FY26 revenue of INR445 crores; existing capacity running at about 80%. Additional 25,000 sq ft planned for custom furnaces this year; land acquired for about INR25 crores in Q1 for cable expansion.
demand_pricing: Pipeline healthy across thermal and nuclear power in India and steel and glass globally; quoted pipeline in Middle East has increased but firm orders still awaited.
OEM order visibility of 9-12 months versus about 4-4.5 months order book for heavy-industry customers; furnace contract is 5 years.
Inventory of INR110-120 crores, 65-70% in raw material; raw materials booked at order receipt and price fluctuations passed through to customers.
Management says Chinese competition is limited for engineered make-to-order products; some customers shifting sourcing to India.
Export share rose to about 34%; new subsidiaries in Mexico, Poland and South Korea; Korean JV supplying battery manufacturing.

qa_highlights.question: How has the fuel cell OEM order trajectory evolved and what run-rate exit FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said field trials and run-up are advanced and focus is now on scaling execution; it declined to quantify exit run-rate, calling it a work in progress.

qa_highlights.question: What share of revenue comes from critical, high-barrier industries?
qa_highlights.answer: Management estimated roughly 75-90% of revenue from critical applications, with 10-20% from regular, more competitive industries; vendor approvals can take 3-5 years.

qa_highlights.question: How big is the new-age industry TAM and its contribution?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not quantify TAM; said new-age products could grow in the high 20s or 30s percent over 2-3 years. Newer products segment addressable market is about INR3,000 crores with less than 1% currently addressed.

qa_highlights.question: What is the margin recovery bridge and timing?
qa_highlights.answer: Employee cost increase reflects headcount added for future projects; margin recovery expected to start in H2 FY27, not FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Middle East/Africa and political situation a risk to revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no negative impact seen in the next few quarters; electrification trend could be positive mid-term.

qa_highlights.question: When will the INR500 crore incremental capacity reach full utilisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Capacity comes online from Q1 FY28 with construction largely done by Q3 FY28; full utilisation expected around FY29-FY30, with plants typically run at about 80% maximum.

financial_highlights.change: +148.8% YoY, low base as heater facility commissioned end of Q1 FY26
+45% YoY, about 140 bps margin impact; includes INR57 lakh ESOP charge in prior-year quarter

This is like a work in progress, and we will come back with the exact results as we execute these projects.

544886|2026-06.management_tone: Management was confident on demand, exports and the long-term pipeline, but cautious and sometimes evasive on quantification: it declined to give fuel cell run-rates, order book size, TAM figures and the Middle East timing. It framed the Q1 margin decline as deliberate investment ahead of projects, with recovery promised for H2 FY27.

rows.why: Management says employee cost is absorbed as revenue catches up and margin recovery starts in H2 FY27, from a Q1 EBITDA margin of 22% versus 25.3% a year earlier and a gross material margin of 47.4% versus 49.3%.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Q1 revenue rose 33% to INR118 cr with Temperature Sensing +42% to INR60 cr and exports +78% to INR39.8 cr, and management guides FY27 growth in line with the ~27% three-year blended rate.

rows.why: Utilisation is about 80% and management has already added a 25,000 sq ft custom furnace expansion this year plus INR25 cr of land bought in Q1 for cable expansion, so further capex is a reasonable expectation.

rows.why: Management guided FY27 revenue growth only in line with the ~27% three-year blended rate and margins broadly similar to FY26, with no sign of a raise; Q1 growth of 33% is partly a low base in Electrical Heating (+148.8%) that fades from Q2.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Q1 EBITDA margin fell to 22% from 25.3% on employee cost up 45% to INR20.4 cr, and recovery is promised only for H2 FY27, so the margin guide could slip if the H2 bridge does not show up.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: EDGE pyrometer series with Micro-Epsilon starts dispatch in Q3 FY27, the cable harness line with UL certification has launched, and heater explosion-proof certification is targeted by Q4 FY27 for the 7.2 kV range.

rows.label: OEM order visibility 9-12 months and 5-year furnace contract
rows.why: OEM order visibility is 9-12 months versus a 4-4.5 month heavy-industry order book, and a 5-year standard furnace supply contract was signed with a life sciences OEM.

rows.label: Export and new subsidiaries (Mexico, Poland, South Korea)
rows.why: Export share rose to about 34% of revenue (INR39.8 cr, +78.3%), new subsidiaries were set up in Mexico, Poland and South Korea, and the Korean JV is supplying battery manufacturers.

rows.label: Lower finance cost from IPO-funded debt repayment
rows.why: INR55 cr of IPO proceeds were used for debt repayment, and management says lower finance cost will be visible from the coming quarter.

tone.note: Management was confident on demand, exports, the pipeline and the INR500 cr capacity plan, but cautious on margins and evasive on quantification, declining to give the fuel cell exit run-rate, order book size, TAM or Middle East timing; analysts pushed on the H2 margin recovery and fuel cell ramp.

544889|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 7% YoY to INR218 crores, while new-business opex drag of INR23 crores left consolidated EBITDA at INR45 crores.
544889|2026-06.overview: Symbiotec's first earnings call after its BSE/NSE listing reported Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue of INR218 crores (+7% YoY), with API revenue of INR215 crores (+6% YoY, volume-led) and API EBITDA of INR66 crores (+9% YoY). Consolidated EBITDA was INR45 crores and net profit about INR14 crores, which management said understates underlying profitability because of INR23 crores of new-business opex and INR11 crores of depreciation that were previously capitalised as pre-operative expenses. No CDMO or injectable revenue was booked in the quarter, versus about INR33 crores of milestone revenue in Q4 FY26. Management reiterated FY27 guidance of roughly 20% revenue growth and 25% EBITDA growth, with a plus/minus 5% band, and pinned new-business revenue to milestones in H2 FY27 and commercial CDMO revenue to the next 6 to 12 months.

financial_highlights.change: About INR326 crores after IPO proceeds of INR142 crores and September-quarter capex

segments.name: API (steroid and hormone APIs)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR215 crores, +6% YoY, driven largely by volume; API EBITDA INR66 crores, +9% YoY; gross margin 60%+. Management says more than 90% of FY27 revenue comes from API. Capacity utilisation is about 70-80%.

segments.name: Biotech CDMO (fermentation)
segments.commentary: No revenue in Q1 FY27. Built on about 400 kL of large-scale fermentation at Ujjain, with signed 10-year take-or-pay with a US alternate-protein player and 5-year take-or-pay for insulin drug substance. Small revenues are guided for Q4 FY27 and meaningful revenues for FY28.

segments.name: Complex injectables (dual-chamber vials/bags)
segments.commentary: No revenue in Q1 FY27 (Q4 FY26 had about INR33 crores of milestone revenue across CDMO and injectables). First DCV ANDA filed in September 2026; second molecule ANDA planned for Q4 FY27. Term sheet with a large US pharma multinational; definitive agreement expected early Q3 FY27.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth of about 20% and EBITDA growth of about 25% on a consolidated basis, with a plus/minus 5% band citing global operating uncertainty.
PAT growth will be lower than EBITDA growth because of depreciation drag; cash PAT (PAT plus depreciation) growth is expected to be above 25%.
New-business opex of about INR23 crores and depreciation of about INR11 crores per quarter to run for the next two to three quarters.
Management expects the first couple of quarters to be lumpy, with a strong H2 FY27 from milestone cash flows (Q3/Q4) that management says will offset the new-business opex.
Insulin/biologics revenue expected to start early FY28, pending stability studies and DCGI approval.
Capex of INR200-250 crores per year for the next two to three years, funded by internal accruals and customer contributions.
capex_capacity: Cumulative investment of more than INR1,000 crores in the two new businesses, of which over INR500 crores is in biomanufacturing/biopharma fermentation.
Gross block in API about INR640 crores as of 30 June 2026; management cites INR800-900 crores of API revenue and asset turnover of about 1.5x.

Phase 0: existing 400 kL fermentation capacity, largely booked under current contracts. Phase 1: brownfield expansion of about 600 kL (about 4x the current capacity) with construction starting Q3 FY27 and 15-18 months to build.
DCV: five to six products developed and moving to plant-level validation; a second DCV line may be needed soon due to capacity constraints.
Mhow injectable facility is part of the roughly INR1,000 crores invested in new businesses.
demand_pricing: Management says demand and traction are very strong, with discussions with more than half a dozen potential customers, each seeking about 1 million litres of fermentation capacity.
Take-or-pay contracts are multi-million-dollar per customer; management declined to disclose per-litre pricing, minimum revenue or contract values, citing confidentiality.
Management guides to industry-level margins for complex injectables and CDMO: gross margin above 70% and EBITDA margin above 35%, and expects Symbiotec to be in a similar range.

API gross margin guided at around 60% (currently above 60%), with EBITDA margin near 30%. Management attributes margin strength to backward integration (make vs buy) and mix shift toward regulated markets.
Customer base: over 200 customers in more than 40 countries; about 70% of FY26 revenue from customers served for more than seven years.

qa_highlights.question: How should capacity, revenue and take-or-pay minimums in the fermentation business be framed over five years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the advanced-stage contracts would require about four times the current capacity (Phase 1, over 2-3 years). It did not give per-litre revenue or minimum revenue numbers, only that each contract is multi-million dollar and asset turnover should exceed 1.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 600 kL expansion for existing or new customers, and what is the capex?
qa_highlights.answer: The 600 kL Phase 1 is tied to a customer with a signed term sheet, with construction starting Q3 FY27 and taking 15-18 months. Funding combines internal accruals with customer contributions; no specific outlay was given beyond INR200-250 crores a year.

qa_highlights.question: What are opex and milestone expectations for the new businesses?
qa_highlights.answer: The INR23 crores quarterly opex run rate should continue for two to three quarters. Management said H2 milestone revenues would offset the full-year new-business opex, without giving amounts.

qa_highlights.question: How long before DCV launches, and how many products follow?
qa_highlights.answer: The first DCV ANDA is filed, the second is due in Q4 FY27, and five to six products are in development. Management said capacity, not product count, is the constraint, and a second line may be needed.

qa_highlights.question: Why was there no revenue from CDMO and injectables in Q1, and what were last year's milestones?
qa_highlights.answer: Milestone revenue is periodic, not quarterly. About INR33 crores was recognised in Q4 FY26, and none in Q1 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What is API capacity utilisation and gross and EBITDA margin sustainability?
qa_highlights.answer: API utilisation is about 70-80%. Management expects gross margin around 60% and EBITDA margin near 30%, with variance from logistics and solvent prices.

qa_highlights.question: Premarin generic timing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give timing, saying the partner controls formulation development and FDA submission; Symbiotec's part is the API.

qa_highlights.question: API share of revenue two years out?
qa_highlights.answer: API is over 90% of revenue today. Management expects it to fall below half in 5-6 years as CDMO and DCV scale.

544890|2026-06.headline: Skyways Q1 FY27 operating revenue rose 90.4% YoY to INR1,216.53 crores, with consolidated PAT margin at 2.2% versus 1.72%.
544890|2026-06.overview: Management reported a strong Q1 FY27, with operating revenue up 90.4% YoY to INR1,216.53 crores and operating EBITDA up to INR50.12 crores from INR27.31 crores. Management attributed much of the revenue jump to per-unit freight cost increases driven by fuel indices, with volume growth of 23% in air cargo and 18% in ocean freight. Employee and other expenses fell as a share of revenue, lifting margins. The company also flagged a board-approved INR30 crore international office expansion and INR20 crore capital infusion into existing overseas subsidiaries, and repaid around INR140 crores of borrowings post-listing.

segments.name: Express

qa_highlights.answer: Management said 23-25% of revenue growth came from volume and the rest from per-unit cost increases driven by fuel indices; it did not give a steady-state figure.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 25-30% volume growth sustainable, and is the realisation growth tied to fuel?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is confident of sustaining volume growth and aims to improve it; yield is market-driven and fuel is a pass-through. Focus is on higher-yield trade lanes.

qa_highlights.question: Gestation period and capex for new Asian offices?
qa_highlights.answer: Historical gestation is 2-4 years; management targets 2-3 years. About 15% of the INR30 crores is capex. Current footprint covers Hong Kong, Thailand, Vietnam, Cambodia and Bangladesh.

qa_highlights.question: Which markets get the INR20 crore subsidiary infusion?
qa_highlights.answer: Subsidiaries in the UAE, Saudi Arabia and Vietnam.

qa_highlights.question: Status of the digital booking platform?
qa_highlights.answer: Air, ocean and express are in pilot; trucking is in final development. Launch expected in 30-60 days.

qa_highlights.question: Update on the EOW matter in the prospectus?

qa_highlights.answer: Management said historical ROE is 14-15%, the September quarter will show the post-listing capital effect, and it targets around 15% over time. About INR140 crores of borrowings were repaid.

544891|2026-06.headline: Hy-Tech Q1 FY27 revenue rose 13% YoY to INR430 million, but EBITDA margin fell to 19.6% from 21.5%, which management blames on price-revision timing.
544891|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations grew 13% YoY to INR430 million and PAT rose 11% to INR46 million, while EBITDA was flat at INR84 million and margin contracted about 190 bps. Management attributed the margin dip to input-cost increases from the Feb–April period whose OEM price revisions, effective 1 April, are expected to be recognised only in Q2, and a cut-off sales shift into the next quarter. This was the company's first earnings call after its 1 September listing on NSE and BSE. Management guided to ~20% revenue growth, 25–30% PAT growth and a 24–25% EBITDA margin for FY27, with capacity expansion and new-customer wins as the main drivers.

segments.commentary: OEMs are 70–80% of business. Management expects domestic business to grow 15–20%, and domestic sales are about INR120–130 crore at present.

segments.commentary: About 10% of business through four distributors (Ahmedabad, Bangalore, Delhi, Pune); management sees 10–30% growth potential here.

Board approved purchase of 6.5 acres of land for a future plant, with acquisition in 3–4 months; plant investment estimated at INR350–500 crore, with a 2–3 year horizon and roughly two times the productivity of current plants.

Total addressable market cited as INR40,000 crore globally (USA INR20,000 crore, Europe INR10,000 crore, India INR2,000 crore, other INR8,000 crore). Management says it holds about 10% of India.
Sany (Chinese excavator maker) approached Hy-Tech to indigenise its fittings supply; management also expects tenders and government-linked OEMs to be added.

Stainless steel fittings for data centres and oil & gas: range developed over 1.5–2 years; management expects revenue in FY28–FY29, with no current customer discussions specified.

544897|2026-09.headline: Paluck Technologies guides FY27 revenue of INR130-140 crores and PAT of INR17-18 crores, about 25% growth, with H1 PAT of about INR5 crores.

Full-year FY27 guidance is INR130-140 crores of revenue and INR17-18 crores of PAT, implying a heavy H2 (about 60% of revenue). Management said IPO proceeds were not yet deployed in H1 and expects their impact in FY28, with FY28 revenue targeted at INR190-200 crores. On the call, operating cash flow was negative (about negative INR9 crores), trade receivables rose about 80% YoY, and H1 operating margin was about 17%, which management attributed to timing and one-off items.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Sharon AI contract structure: five or seven years?

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the INR 670 crore non-current and INR 1,900 crore current liabilities on the balance sheet?

qa_highlights.question: What are the India capex, capacity and revenue targets?

544901|2026-06.headline: Purple Style Labs Q1 FY27 revenue rose to INR119 crores (from INR106 crores), but EBITDA was negative INR11 crores vs negative INR4 crores a year earlier.
544901|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 was the first full quarter with the four large-format experience centres opened in FY26 (Fort Mumbai, South Ex Delhi, Linking Road Bandra, Madison Avenue New York). GMV rose to INR193 crores from INR133 crores and AOV rose to INR86,000 from INR66,000. Revenue from operations was INR119 crores, gross margin held at 36%, and EBITDA and PAT losses were wider than a year earlier on the higher fixed cost base of the new stores. Inventory and net working capital fell year on year, but borrowings rose to INR436 crores at June 2026 from INR371 crores at FY26 end.

segments.name: Mumbai (3M FY27)
segments.commentary: Contribution rose to INR50 crores from INR28 crores in the first three months of FY26. Mumbai was the largest market in FY26 GMV at INR205 crores.

segments.name: Delhi (3M FY27)
segments.commentary: Contribution rose to INR39 crores from INR29 crores. Delhi FY26 GMV was INR166 crores.

segments.name: Hyderabad (3M FY27)
segments.commentary: Contribution rose to INR16 crores from INR10 crores.

segments.name: USA (3M FY27)
segments.commentary: Contribution rose to INR29 crores from INR20 crores. New York flagship opened in March 2026 and is the first US store; US was online-only before that.

guidance_outlook: No objective margin or profitability guidance given; management said it would refrain from it.
Q1 is the leanest quarter; management said the cost structure set in Q1 will carry into Q2 absent changes, and clearer trends are expected over the next two quarters.
No significant new experience centre expansion is planned near term; the first full year of the FY26 store investments is to be observed.

EBITDA break-even framing: on a P&L basis, gross profit of about INR55 crores would be needed for zero EBITDA, with lease-related costs of INR45 crores (lease interest plus ROU depreciation) included. On a cash basis, lease payments of INR29 crores imply a smaller gap.
Lease interest and ROU depreciation are expected to stay broadly flat unless stores change. Other finance cost should decline as operating profit reduces debt.
capex_capacity: Four large-format experience centres opened in FY26: Fort Mumbai and South Ex Delhi (operational since Q2 FY26), Linking Road Bandra (end-March 2026), and Madison Avenue New York (March 2026).
Store footprint is organised by geography, not by store, so same-store sales are not tracked. Mumbai now runs two large-format centres.
The New York lease is a June-end lease with a shorter tenure, so rent can be adjusted after 12-18 months of performance.
Inventory is expected to stay roughly flat at the current level absent further expansion. Management said inventory is around INR160 crores, with breadth-led singular-unit stock.
demand_pricing: AOV rose to INR86,000 in Q1 FY27, from INR76,000 in FY26 and INR46,000 in FY24. Store AOV is about 2.5x online AOV (India online about INR38,000 vs store about INR90,000 in FY26).
Active designer brands fell to 1,109 in FY26 from 1,910 in FY24. Top 100 designers were 67% of sales in FY24.
Average GMV per customer rose to INR108,000 in FY26 from INR67,000 in FY24. Top 50,000 customers contributed INR702 crores of FY26 GMV of INR722 crores.
Women's wear above INR1 lakh grew to INR312 crores GMV in FY26 from INR187 crores in FY24. Women's wear below INR35,000 fell to INR86 crores from INR162 crores.
Gross margin percentage is said to be broadly flat across price points. Management argued that absolute gross profit per piece rises with higher ticket size.

qa_highlights.question: Why is operating cash flow still negative and borrowings rising despite lower inventory and working capital? When does the business become self-funded?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the lower inventory reflects better inventory management after the FY22-25 build-up, and higher customer advances (INR49 crores) helped working capital. Debt is funding interest costs, and Q1 is not operationally profitable. It asked investors to observe the next few quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Does the higher-ticket strategy improve gross margin or only AOV?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said percentage gross margin is similar across categories. The benefit is in absolute gross profit per piece (e.g., at 40% margin a INR2 lakh piece yields INR80,000 vs INR8,000 for a INR20,000 piece), plus lower supply and customer complexity from the long tail.

qa_highlights.question: What is the split of outright purchase, consignment and backorder inventory?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said consignment split is business-sensitive and not disclosed. Outright purchase forms the inventory on the books. Backorder advances are about one month of revenue, and average delivery is 45-60 days, so backorder customer advances are not inventory.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for finance costs in FY27 and FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Lease interest plus ROU depreciation (INR45 crores in the P&L) should stay at Q1 levels absent new store changes. Other finance cost should fall as operating profit reduces debt.

qa_highlights.question: What GMV scale, gross margin and operating leverage are needed for EBITDA positivity?
qa_highlights.answer: On an EBITDA basis, gross profit of about INR55 crores would be needed. Adding the lease costs of INR45 crores (P&L) or INR29 crores (cash) raises the required gross profit. Management referred to the detailed P&L on slide 20.

qa_highlights.question: What is the New York store's AOV and break-even, and what is the SSG for mature stores?
qa_highlights.answer: Management estimated a New York store AOV of about INR1.25 lakh (about USD1,500), based on a 2.5x multiple to online AOV. It did not give a break-even GMV. Same-store growth is not tracked because the company reports by geography.

qa_highlights.question: What is the real jewellery contribution and London store capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Real jewellery is sold from some stores and raises AOV; it is not separately disclosed and will appear as a line item only when sizable (example given: about INR100 crores). London upgrade has no firm timeline and capex is in line with the overall ratio.

capex_capacity: Five projects in progress: new 100K sq ft Gen 4 Delhi flagship, upgrades of Ahmedabad, Kolkata and Bangalore to Gen 3 (each targeted at 10,000-20,000 sq ft, eventually 20,000+), and London upgrade from Gen 1 to Gen 3 with no firm timeline; nothing signed as of the call.

Capex plus deposits estimated at INR80-90 crores over the next 18 months to March 2028 for the five projects (INR75-80 crores in one earlier estimate; INR80-85 crores over 3 years in another answer); management said the 2.5 lakh sq ft existing footprint represents about INR150 crores of capex plus deposits, used as the scaling ratio.

Company currently has about 2.5 lakh sq ft across stores and 14 stores in 11 cities, including London and New York; four large-format stores opened in Mumbai, Delhi and New York in the recent period, with Linking Road and New York opened March-April 2026.
New York store lease runs to June 27 (short lease taken because it was a new geography); management will decide on renewal, renegotiation or exit and will answer on the Q3 call.

Cash fixed cost base of about INR360-370 crores a year; quarterly cash spend about INR85-90 crores; P&L cost base about INR100 crores per quarter, with about INR15 crores a quarter difference from cash basis, mainly ROU depreciation of about INR45 crores vs cash rent of about INR30-31 crores.
demand_pricing: H1 FY27 GMV INR397 crores vs INR310 crores; average order value INR84,000 vs INR69,000; revenue from operations INR262 crores vs INR214 crores.
Mumbai H1 FY27 GMV INR105 crores vs INR77 crores; FY26 Mumbai GMV INR205 crores (INR77 crores H1, INR128 crores H2); management implies INR250 crores+ for FY27 on a 40:60 split and about 30% growth.
Delhi H1 FY27 GMV INR85 crores; FY30 Delhi target INR700 crores with new 100K sq ft Gen 4 flagship.

USA H1 FY27 GMV INR64 crores vs INR42 crores; store AOV above $1,500 vs about $500 online; management declined to split store vs online GMV, citing omnichannel and migration from online to store; pre-store US online GMV was about INR100-120 crores a year.

Market context: top 1,000 designer brands market over INR10,000 crores, expected to reach INR25,000 crores by 2030 per cited industry projection, growing about 20-21%; company's share rose from 2% (2020) to 6% (2025), target 8%+ by 2030. Management said a 15% market growth would still allow INR2,100 crores with 10.5% share.

Designer-wear customer penetration target 25% by 2030 (20% in 2025); wallet share target 34% by 2030 (32% in 2025). Revenue-to-GMV conversion about 80% plus or minus 3% annually; H1 about 66%, Q2 about 70%.

Gross margin improved in Q1 and Q2; management expects FY27 gross margin above FY26. Real jewellery sold from some stores, not inventory-funded; not separately disclosed. Backorders (customer pays 100% upfront, 2-12 week delivery) keep net working capital low: inventory INR196 crores, NWC about INR60 crores.
risks_watch: Profitability: H1 FY27 EBITDA still a loss of about INR7 crores; gross profit must cross roughly INR360-370 crores a year on a cash basis, with the company targeting most of the gap in FY27 and full bridging in FY28.
H2 delivery: management implies H2 GMV about 30% above H1 and attributes a Q2 wedding-shopping delay to Q3 and Q4; any shortfall would weigh on the FY27 view.
New York lease expires June 27 (2027); renewal, renegotiation or exit decision due on the Q3 call. US GMV and store economics remain short-track.
Execution on five projects with nothing signed as of the call; London and Ahmedabad/Kolkata/Bangalore timelines unfixed; Delhi Gen 4 flagship not yet located.

Cash and interest: management expects no operating cash losses in H2 and lower interest after IPO proceeds, but did not quantify; net working capital and inventory (INR196 crores) need to keep falling.
Macro and demand: festive-season shift and lower destination-wedding travel flagged in media; management called them minor but has not quantified.

Data consistency: several transcript corrections are noted (luxury market size, slide references) and some capex figures varied across answers (INR75-80 crores, INR80-85 crores, INR80-90 crores), so the basis should be confirmed.
key_quotes: So what tends to happen, let's say Mumbai stores do a certain number in the first financial year, which is FY27.
So let's say today if my annual expenses are in the range of INR360 crores, INR370 crores on a cash basis, once I cross INR360 crores, INR370 crores of GP, that means we become profitable from there.
So I think so long as we are able to reduce this net working capital going forward it would actually amplify our capital efficiency in this business versus any other platform.
But I think if there is any such headwind due to geopolitical issues, our New York store will compensate for that.
544901|2026-09.management_tone: Confident on the long-term FY30 GMV target and on Mumbai and US throughput, but cautious and non-committal on quarterly numbers, the New York lease, and the timing of the new projects, repeatedly declining to give quarterly guidance or store-level margins.

rows.label: Margin expansion

rows.why: Real jewellery is already sold from some stores and is not separately disclosed (example scale about INR100 crores), and the Gen 3 and Gen 4 store formats are rolling out, but no specific new product launch was named.

rows.why: Cash fixed cost base is INR360-370 crores a year (quarterly cash spend INR85-90 crores), so incremental gross profit flows to EBITDA once the threshold is crossed; H1 FY27 EBITDA was still a loss of about INR7 crores.

544903|2026-09.headline: Deepa Jewellers Q2 FY27 revenue rose 25% YoY to INR 626 crore, but EBITDA margin fell to 7.24% on plain-gold mix and PAT rose 37% to INR 37 crore.
544903|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue from operations grew 25% YoY to INR 626 crore, with EBITDA of INR 45 crore (up 17% YoY, margin 7.24%) and PAT of INR 37 crore (up 37%, margin 5.96%). H1 FY27 revenue rose 30% to INR 1,057 crore, EBITDA rose 24% to INR 84 crore (7.95% margin) and PAT rose 32% to INR 64 crore. Management attributed the Q2 growth moderation to festive demand shifting into H2, and said lower gross margin came from a plain-gold-heavy sales mix, with PAT supported by other income and a lower tax rate. The company also commenced its in-house Hyderabad manufacturing facility in September 2026 and guided to 40-45% revenue CAGR for FY27-FY29.

segments.name: Job work
segments.commentary: Volume of 318 kg in Q2 (+44% YoY) and 544 kg in H1 (+51% YoY). Realisation per gram fell to about INR 178-180 from about INR 200 a year earlier, which management attributed to plain-gold mix rather than pricing changes.

segments.name: Jewellery manufacturing (invoice/own gold)
segments.commentary: Volume of 491 kg in Q2 (broadly stable) and 783 kg in H1 (-5% YoY). Own-processing realisation fell to about INR 12,600/g from INR 14,500/g, attributed to lower gold prices, plain-gold mix and higher 18-karat sales.

segments.name: Studded vs plain gold mix
segments.commentary: Studded share was 57% of H1 FY27 sales, against 65% in FY26, with plain gold at 43%. Management targets studded share of 75% over the next three to four quarters.

guidance_outlook: Revenue CAGR of 40-45% guided for FY27, FY28 and FY29, with FY27 growth of 40-45% compared with FY26 (March 2026) base; the 40-45% figure was also described as a 40-50% revenue CAGR for two years at a constant 24-karat gold rate of INR 50,000.
EBITDA margin expected to expand 80-120 bps over the next 4-6 quarters, driven by the Hyderabad facility, Tier-2/3 expansion, studded mix and standalone store sales.
Gross margin pressure from plain-gold mix expected to normalise in upcoming quarters.
Hedging to rise from 94% toward close to 100% of gold holdings over the next two to three quarters.
Working capital cycle (inventory days plus receivable days) expected in the 55-65 day range; inventory and receivables expected to normalise from Q3.
Internal accruals, IPO proceeds and existing debt expected to fund growth through FY29.
Effective tax rate guided at the standard 25.168%; Q2 benefit came from deferred tax on IPO expenses, with the tax shield reversing in later years.
capex_capacity: In-house manufacturing facility in Hyderabad, about 6,700 sq ft, commenced operations in September 2026.
Facility capacity of about 1.5 tonnes a year on single shift and about 2.5 tonnes a year on double shift.
Facility processed 65 kg (13% of volume) in Q1 FY27 and 167 kg (21%) in Q2 FY27; management expects about 40% in Q3 and about 50% in Q4.
Second sales office in Chennai planned for December 2026; Bangalore office planned for April-May 2027, following Vijayawada office.
Long-run target mix of 65% in-house and 35% outsourced manufacturing; outsourced work to shift in-house from Q4 FY27.
demand_pricing: Revenue concentrated in South India (Telangana, Andhra Pradesh, Tamil Nadu, Karnataka, Kerala); client base about 373 customers including 47 jewellery retail chains such as Joyalukkas, Kalyan, Lalitha and Bhima.
Q2 growth moderated as festive demand shifted into H2; H1 typically contributes about 40% of annual revenue.
Retail customers shifting from cash purchases to old-gold exchange after a gold price spike, moving sales from invoice basis to job work; management said total volume shifted rather than fell.

Job work conversion margin is about 75% and invoice-basis about 8%, with a similar ROCE/ROE in both models; job work is priced at about 1% lower wastage (4% vs 5%) because it needs no working capital.
Gold price assumption for guidance: constant 24-karat rate of INR 50,000 per 10 g; average selling gold price rose from about INR 8,000/g in FY25 to INR 11,950/g in FY26.

qa_highlights.question: Why did gross margin and grammage realisation decline in Q2, and why did job work realisation drop about 10%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the change was a shift toward plain gold jewellery (lower margin than studded), not a strategic or operational change, and expects normalisation. Job work realisation fell to about INR 178 from INR 202 a year earlier (about 11%), attributed to the same SKU mix.

qa_highlights.question: Why did inventory and receivable days rise versus March 2026?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said March is not a like-for-like base because year-end corporate purchases stop; higher inventory came from stock built for the new Vijayawada sales office in September after IPO proceeds. Management expects normalisation from Q3 and a combined inventory plus receivable cycle of 55-65 days.

qa_highlights.question: What is the revenue outlook for the next 2-3 years?
qa_highlights.answer: Growth to come from new geographies (Vijayawada, Chennai, Bangalore offices), SKU expansion into studded casting, Nakshi and Tapa jewellery (16 SKUs launched in Q1), and client store expansion including franchise models. Guidance is 40-45% CAGR for FY27-FY29.

qa_highlights.question: What is the margin impact of the new facility, and what EBITDA margin should be expected?
qa_highlights.answer: Depreciation and karigar costs weighed on Q1 and Q2 margins; benefit expected from Q3 as more volume shifts in-house. Management guided to an 80-120 bps EBITDA margin expansion over 4-6 quarters, with a note that studded mix and standalone store sales also contribute.

qa_highlights.question: How is gold price exposure hedged, and what is the target?
qa_highlights.answer: 94% of gold holdings were hedged as of 30 September through gold metal loans (3.25% p.a.), MCX short futures and back-to-back unfixed purchases from bullion suppliers. Target is close to 100% within two to three quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the effective tax rate fall to about 15%, and will it normalise?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said the standard rate is 25.168%; the lower Q2 rate reflects deferred tax on IPO expenses, which Companies Act treats against securities premium while Income Tax allows over five years. The effect is expected to even out in later years.

qa_highlights.question: Will promoters draw salary, and how will they be compensated?
qa_highlights.answer: Both Ashish Agarwal and Dev Agarwal will not draw salary from 1 October 2026, and Dev Agarwal said no salary is planned for at least 10 quarters, after which the board will decide.

risks_watch: Gross margin and realisation pressure from plain-gold mix and lower gold prices; management quantified a 50% gold price fall at about 60 bps gross margin impact.
Working capital intensity: inventory and receivable days rose versus September FY26, and growth of 40-45% needs funding from accruals, IPO proceeds and debt.
Execution risk on new Hyderabad plant ramp-up (targeted about 40% of volume in Q3 and 50% in Q4) and on Chennai and Bangalore office launches.
Shift of retail customers toward old-gold exchange could keep invoice-basis sales subdued and raise job work share.
Customer concentration in South India and in a few large jewellery chains.
Tax rate normalisation from Q2 deferred benefit back to 25.168%.
Hedging coverage to rise to close to 100%; monitor in next quarter.
544903|2026-09.management_tone: Confident on growth and margin recovery, with management repeatedly describing Q2 softness as a mix and timing effect. Management was more evasive on specifics, notably the EBITDA margin direction (a live misstatement of 80-120 bps versus a dip was clarified on the call) and on the basis for the 40-45% CAGR. Answers on the old-gold shift and inventory build were detailed and conceded the points.
key_quotes: So, from the 3rd Quarter onwards, both the promoters will not be drawing any salary from the business.
It is just a change in the SKU mix which is expected to normalize in the upcoming quarters.
But yes, I accept that there has been a slight increase in the inventory days as well as the trade receivable days when we compare it to the numbers of September Fiscal '26.
So, over the next 4-5 quarters, we expect about 80-120 bps increase in our EBITDA margins over a period of next 4-6 quarters.
Sir, it is not a dip sir, I mentioned that our EBITDA margin will increase by 80 to 120 basis points.

As of now, I as promoter of the company on a personal front have sufficient liquidity and as we are more inclined to the faster growth of the company, currently we have no plans of drawing any kind of salary at least for 10 quarters from now.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management guided 80-120 bps EBITDA margin expansion over 4-6 quarters from Hyderabad in-house shift, Tier-2/3 expansion and studded mix (57% of H1 sales vs 65% FY26, target 75% in 3-4 quarters), but Q2 margin fell to 7.24% and H1 margin is 7.95%.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.when: Q3 FY27 onward (Chennai Dec 2026, Bangalore Apr-May 2027)
rows.why: Hyderabad facility commenced Sept 2026 (1.5 t/yr single shift, 2.5 t/yr double shift), with in-house share targeted at 40% of volume in Q3 and 50% in Q4 from 21% in Q2; Chennai office dated Dec 2026 and Bangalore Apr-May 2027.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Total operating volume grew 13% YoY to 809 kg in Q2 and 12% to 1,327 kg in H1, with job work up 44% in Q2; processing/manufacturing was flat (-5% in H1), and festive demand is expected in H2.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation was not disclosed; the single-shift Hyderabad plant has 1.5 t/yr capacity with 167 kg processed in Q2, and the company plans a 65% in-house target, so further capacity could be needed, but no new capex was guided.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Q2 revenue growth slowed to 25% YoY from H1's 30%, and the 40-45% CAGR is not tied to specific orders, so there is no sign of a guidance raise yet.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Growth decelerated from 30% in H1 to 25% in Q2, the Hyderabad ramp (21% to 50% of volume by Q4) and working capital (55-65 day cycle) are execution risks, and the 40-45% CAGR is not backed by specific orders.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Studded casting, Nakshi and Tapa jewellery SKUs were launched (16 SKUs in Q1), and management cited SKU expansion as a growth driver, but no specific new launch dates were given beyond those.

rows.label: Inventory plus receivable cycle back to 55-65 days
rows.why: Management said inventory and receivables will normalise from Q3 and expects a combined cycle of 55-65 days, with higher inventory tied to stock built for the Vijayawada office after IPO proceeds.

rows.label: Gold hedging rising to near 100%
rows.why: Hedging rose to 94% of gold holdings at 30 September from 75% over 2-3 years, with a stated aim of close to 100% in 2-3 quarters, which cuts price risk.

rows.label: Gross margin normalisation from plain-gold mix
rows.why: Job work realisation fell to about INR 178/g from about INR 200/g and own-processing to INR 12,600/g from INR 14,500/g; management expects normalisation, but a 50% gold price fall would cut gross margin about 60 bps.

tone.note: Management was confident on the 40-45% CAGR, the Hyderabad ramp and margin recovery, and described Q2 softness as mix and timing; analysts pressed on the margin direction, the basis for the CAGR, the low tax rate, and the inventory build.

544911|2026-06.headline: Kanohar Q1 FY27 revenue rose 103.5% YoY to INR137.1 crore, with EBITDA margin of 28.3% and order book of about INR2,026 crore.
544911|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations was INR137.1 crore, up 103.5% YoY, with transformers at 84.9% and EPC at 14.81% of revenue. EBITDA rose 152.2% to INR38.8 crore (28.3% margin, up 550 bps) and PAT rose 140% to INR27.3 crore (19.9% margin). Consolidated order book stood at about INR2,026 crore on June 30, 2026, up 11% from March 31, 2026, after incremental orders of INR332.2 crore in Q1 and INR867.3 crore in Q2 to date. Management guided FY27 revenue of about INR950 crore with EBITDA margin similar to FY26, with H2 as the main execution period.

financial_highlights.value: Q1: INR332.2 crore; Q2 to date: INR867.3 crore

segments.name: Power Transformers / 400 kV
segments.commentary: 400 kV transformers contributed 70.16% of Q1 revenue (52% in FY26, 10.3% in FY24). Management said 400 kV, Scott-connected and shunt reactor products carry similar gross margins; about 70% of order book is power transformers, mostly 400 kV.

segments.name: EPC
segments.commentary: EPC contributed 14.81% of Q1 revenue. Management does not disclose EBITDA separately; directionally lower than transformer margins.

segments.name: By end-user
segments.commentary: Power Transmission 85.18%, Railways 11.53%, Renewable Energy 2.84%, Power Distribution 0.23% of Q1 revenue. Shunt reactors were about 13.1% of order book at June 30.

segments.name: Voltage mix (other)
segments.commentary: 132 kV to below 220 kV at 11.38%, 220 kV to below 400 kV at 3.19%, below 132 kV at 0.23% of Q1 revenue.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue target of about INR950 crore, with EBITDA margin broadly similar to FY26.
FY28 revenue growth expected to be similar to FY27 guidance (about 40-45% per analyst's read, not confirmed by management).
Brownfield expansion of about 18,000 MVA at Gangol, targeted to be in place by end-FY28 / FY29; existing capacity seen sufficient through FY28.
Net working capital guided at 110-120 days.
Order book at end-FY27 may be adequate to cover FY28 and FY29 revenue, per management; no specific FY27 closing order book number given.
Shunt reactors expected to be about 10-15% of revenue on average over time.
capex_capacity: Existing capacity about 19,200 MVA across Rithani and Gangol (Meerut); Gangol about 18,000 MVA.
Q1 FY27 executed about 1,725 MVA, implying roughly 36-46% utilisation depending on base used.
Planned brownfield expansion of about 18,000 MVA at Gangol; part funded from IPO proceeds.
765 kV: technology developed in-house; capacity to be suitable for 765 kV; management estimates 3-4 years to become eligible for regular 765 kV tenders.
About 2,500 kW solar plant planned, partly funded from IPO proceeds; savings not quantified.
demand_pricing: Management estimates India 400 kV transformer market at about 60,000-70,000 MVA last year, growing 10-15% industry-wide; analyst's INR4,000-6,000 crore 400 kV market size was confirmed as 'in that range'.
Railways envisages about 1,000 traction substations for high-speed rail over 5-10 years (about 2,000 transformers), implying about INR20,000 crore opportunity.
Most contracts have price variation clauses (IEEMA PVC), which management says offsets raw material swings; order book margins said to be similar to FY26.
Industry lead times are 18-24 months; tenders being bid are mainly for FY29-FY30 execution.
Revenue per MVA about INR6.1 lakh last year; may have risen slightly due to raw material costs.
Management said there were no new entrants in the last 3-6 months that it is aware of, but expects new entrants over time.

qa_highlights.question: How were transformer margins protected in Q1 given input cost increases and fixed-price contracts?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said most contracts carry price variation linked to the IEEMA clause, which passes through raw material moves in both directions.

qa_highlights.question: Will GEC-III drive a multi-year order tailwind for 400 kV and 500 MVA transformers?
qa_highlights.answer: Management called it a multi-decadal structural tailwind; intra-state transmission is mostly 400 kV, but no split of GEC-III capacity by voltage was given.

qa_highlights.question: Can order book reach INR3,000 crore by FY27 end, and 40-45% YoY growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to confirm; said Q2 execution will reduce the order book slightly, and end-FY27 book may cover FY28-FY29 revenue.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 1H-weak, 2H-heavy revenue pattern a continuing trend?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, management said H1 is typically softer and H2 heavier, an industry trend.

qa_highlights.question: Will new 400 kV capacity pressure margins beyond 3-4 years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects visibility for 3-4 years from current order book and tenders; beyond that, short-term supply-demand mismatch and margin pressure are possible.

qa_highlights.question: Why was FY24 a revenue decline and why is utilisation low; are exports planned?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said FY24 focus went to obtaining 400 kV and Scott certifications; ramp-up takes time. Exports are not the current focus; a re-look may come in 3-4 years.

risks_watch: Supply chain and raw material availability, which management named as the key risk; geopolitical sourcing issues were raised.
Margin pressure from new 400 kV entrants and added capacity beyond the 3-4 year visibility window.
Execution timing: H2-weighted revenue and 18-24 month execution cycles.
Capacity addition: brownfield 18,000 MVA must come on stream by FY28-FY29 to support growth.
Order book lumpiness toward power transformers, with large CPSU orders (INR250 crore+) in Q2.
Working capital intensity of 110-120 net days.
Management did not disclose bid pipeline, EBITDA by segment, or the MVA-based breakdown beyond Q1 execution.
544911|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on demand and qualifications, with a clear long-term structural narrative. Cautious and evasive on specifics: declined to confirm order book targets, FY28 growth, bid pipeline, and solar savings, and deferred several answers to later follow-up.

Right now, we are seeing a stable margin profile.

544912|2026-06.headline: Prasol Q1 FY27 revenue rose 35.7% YoY to INR433.6 crores and EBITDA to INR90.3 crores, helped by one-off inventory gains of about INR25 crores.

Management attributed about INR25 crores of gross profit to a sharp rise in selling prices from West Asia-linked supply disruptions and inventory bought at lower prices, which it called partly non-structural. FY27 guidance of INR1,550-1,650 crores revenue and INR240-250 crores adjusted EBITDA excludes these gains, and management described a 15-16% year-end EBITDA margin. A Phase 1 capex of INR250-300 crores for existing products (about 60,000 tpa of added capacity) was outlined.

544912|2026-09.headline: Prasol Q2 FY27 revenue hit a record INR413 crore (+38.6% YoY) and EBITDA INR58 crore (+86.1%), with FY27 guidance reiterated.
544912|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue from operations was INR413 crore, up 38.6% YoY, driven mainly by higher realisations with single-digit domestic volume growth. EBITDA rose 86.1% to INR58 crore and PAT rose 122.2% to INR38 crore. H1 FY27 EBITDA of INR148 crore included a one-time INR25 crore inventory gain and INR0.92 crore forex gain in Q1, and management said underlying full-year EBITDA should be INR240-250 crore. Working capital cycle lengthened from 63 to 76 days as the company added shorter-credit suppliers, and H1 operating cash flow was negative.

qa_highlights.question: Why is H1 operating cash flow negative, and what is the full-year outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said H1 cash flow is a snapshot and the working capital build reflects new suppliers, higher inventory cost and longer shipping times. Management expects inventory to normalise by end Q3 and expects to rebuild inventory in Q4 if demand holds.

qa_highlights.question: What are plant utilisation levels and which industries are targeted by expansion?
qa_highlights.answer: Combined utilisation of both plants is about 65-75%. Expansions cover every non-agro product, with increases of 30-100%. Forward integration and identical plants for lubricant grades are planned.

qa_highlights.answer: CFO said growth came from higher realisations, with single-digit volume growth in the domestic business.
