rows.why: FY27 revenue guidance is only reiterated at INR1,550-1,650 crore and EBITDA at INR240-250 crore, and management declined to give FY28 numbers citing geopolitical uncertainty.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Working capital is 76 days against a 60-70 day target, H1 operating cash flow was negative, freight is up 2.5-3x to the US, and export share is about 25% versus a 30%+ target.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Lubricant additive volume ramp-up is sold out, antibacterial drug re-approval takes 3-6 months, and mining chemicals move to mine-wise trials and bidding with a breakthrough expected within about 2.5 years.

rows.label: Agro sales growth and new molecule exposure
rows.why: October agro sales grew 150% and agro is about 15-16% of revenue, but management says no further agro investment is planned and one molecule has only two Indian manufacturers.

rows.label: Working capital normalisation to 60-70 days
rows.why: Cycle lengthened from 63 to 76 days in Q2 and management expects inventory to normalise by end Q3 FY27, though it plans to rebuild inventory in Q4 if demand holds.

rows.label: Captive renewable power at Mahad
rows.why: A own grid cable costing INR2.5-3 crore is due in 1.5-2 months, against current Mahad power at INR9-9.5 per unit and expected savings of INR1.25-1.50 per unit subject to solar regulations.

tone.note: Management was confident on record Q2 results, reiterated FY27 guidance and the order book, and was cautious and vague on FY28 and the 5-year margin; analysts pressed on inventory risk if crude falls, negative H1 operating cash flow, and the sustainability of the one-time Q1 gain.

544913|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 revenue rose 36% YoY to Rs.107 crore and EBITDA rose 9% to Rs.23 crore, with margin at 21.3% and a Rs.982 crore order book.
544913|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations was Rs.107 crore, up 36% YoY, led by domestic facade (Rs.62 crore, +93%) and fenestration (Rs.6 crore, +127%), while international fell 12% to Rs.39 crore on delivery timing. EBITDA grew 9% to Rs.23 crore, and margin fell to 21.3% because of lower international contribution and a shift to DDP freight billing at cost. Management attributed about 1.5 points of the margin gap to freight pass-through and said the underlying margin is in line with FY26. PAT of Rs.17 crore grew more slowly than EBITDA due to lower other income (prior-year property sale gain) and higher depreciation from new capacity. Management reiterated FY27 guidance of about 25% revenue growth, 23-25% EBITDA margin and 18-20% PAT margin, while flagging a weak first half and a heavier Q3 and Q4.

financial_highlights.change: Lower YoY; international margin cited at 36.3%
Grew slower than EBITDA; lower other income and higher depreciation

financial_highlights.metric: Freight cost included in revenue and cost
financial_highlights.change: Pass-through; adds about 1.5 pts to margin if excluded

segments.name: Domestic facade (turnkey, Grade A developers)
segments.commentary: Q1 revenue Rs.62 crore, up 93% YoY; all order book is commercial real estate in Tier 1 cities. Historically about 49% of FY26 revenue.

segments.name: International facade (B2B product supply, US and Australia)
segments.commentary: Q1 revenue Rs.39 crore, down 12% YoY on delivery timing; management expects Q3 and Q4 to be stronger with three projects. Historically about 45% of FY26 revenue; FY26 Australia revenue was Rs.24 crore.

segments.name: Fenestration (luxury doors and windows)
segments.commentary: Q1 revenue Rs.6 crore, up 127% YoY on luxury residential demand. Historically about 6% of FY26 revenue. Higher margin, lower volume.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth of about 25% YoY (management also cited a 20-25% CAGR ambition).
FY27 EBITDA margin of 23-25% and PAT margin of 18-20% on a consolidated basis, with freight pass-through expected to have limited impact.
Revenue mix for FY27 to stay similar to FY26 (about 49% domestic, 45% international, 6% fenestration).
Glass processing unit commissioning expected in about 8 months, with an estimated 1-1.5% EBITDA margin benefit.
Target of at least 2 years of order book visibility.
capex_capacity: Vile Bhagad (Mangaon) plant on a 1 lakh sq m owned MIDC plot; about 32,000 sq m built to date and about 30% of land used.
Current capacity about 130 panels a day across four production lines, with about 350 workers (about 120 on payroll).
Glass processing unit under construction; total project cost Rs.80 crore, funded by Rs.50 crore fresh issue and internal accruals; commissioning in about 8 months.
Management says infrastructure supports growth for the next couple of years without incremental capex.
In-house NABL-accredited test facility for air, water, seismic, structural and movement testing.
demand_pricing: Order book Rs.982 crore as on 31 July 2026, with no substantial new orders in the past three months; a few near-closure international jobs in the US, Canada and Israel.
Domestic facade market about Rs.9,000 crore, projected to reach about Rs.14,500 crore by FY30 (about 15.9% CAGR, per management).
Management estimates a 6-7% domestic market share, and says it is the second-largest domestic player by revenue.
Contracts include aluminium and glass pass-through across all verticals; freight now billed at cost under DDP terms.
Payment terms are milestone-based (about 10% advance, about 55-60% on material delivery, balance on installation); export invoicing is at dispatch with 60-day credit.
Management said US tariffs could slow US construction demand, but it views the impact on its business as small.

qa_highlights.question: What was Q1 order inflow, and will the freight change and any Q1 delays affect Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no substantial new order came in over the past three months. Freight of about Rs.5.5 crore is a pass-through, and adjusting for it plus the prior-year property gain, margin is in line with FY26. Export is back-ended, with three projects due in Q3 and Q4.

qa_highlights.question: Why has margin risen above pre-COVID levels on lower revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited the export and fenestration verticals, a shift from residential to commercial projects with faster realisations, pass-through clauses on aluminium and glass, and consolidation from three factories to one.

qa_highlights.question: What is the glass processing unit timeline and benefit?
qa_highlights.answer: Commissioning is expected in about 8 months, with an estimated 1-1.5% bottom-line margin benefit.

qa_highlights.question: What is the order-book and growth outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management aims to keep at least 2 years of visibility and grow revenue at 20-25% CAGR; a typical order cycle is 18-24 months (export about 12 months, domestic about 24).

qa_highlights.question: What are the market share and competitive position?
qa_highlights.answer: Management estimates about 6-7% domestic share and says it is second-largest by revenue; its direct competitors are three or four players with revenue around Rs.200 crore.

risks_watch: Seasonality: management said the first two quarters are typically slow, so FY27 delivery depends on the heavier Q3 and Q4.
Order inflow: no substantial new orders in the three months to July, and the company is relying on near-closure international wins.
Freight and duty pass-through: under DDP terms the company bears freight and any tariff changes, and mitigation depends on clients accepting pass-through; management said margin % may dilute.
US demand: management said tariffs could slow US construction demand.
Glass processing unit commissioning in about 8 months; the margin benefit is estimated at 1-1.5%.
544913|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on margin and FY27 guidance, which management reiterated despite the quarter's margin dip. Somewhat evasive on order inflow, export margin split and forward mix, and it repeatedly asked investors to judge on a yearly basis rather than quarterly.
key_quotes: So the margin hasn't deteriorated at all to that extent. It is at par with what we have delivered over the last financial year and what we are committing to deliver this year.
I encourage all the investors today on call to look at this business from a long -term perspective at a yearly level, as opposed to quarterly levels
today, we are a debt-free company, right?

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: EBITDA margin fell to 21.3% in Q1 and FY27 guide is 23-25%, so expansion needs the Q3/Q4 mix and the glass processing unit (1-1.5% benefit) to deliver; freight pass-through costs about 1.5 pts of margin in Q1.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.when: Q2 FY28 (about 8 months from the call)
rows.why: Glass processing unit (Rs.80 crore, under construction) is due for commissioning in about 8 months, while the Vile Bhagad plant has only about 30% of its 1 lakh sq m land used and management says current infrastructure is enough for the next couple of years.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Q1 revenue was Rs.107 crore (+36% YoY) but international fell 12% to Rs.39 crore, and no substantial new orders came in over three months; the Rs.982 crore order book (almost 2x FY26 revenue) supports the heavier Q3/Q4 but is not yet converting to new volume.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation was not disclosed and management says infrastructure supports growth for two years without incremental capex, so a new capex announcement is not signalled, though the Rs.80 crore glass unit is already raised.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management reiterated FY27 guidance of about 25% revenue growth and 23-25% EBITDA margin, but Q1 EBITDA grew only 9% and margin fell to 21.3%, with a weak H1 flagged.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Q1 margin was 21.3% against a 23-25% FY27 target and a weak first half is flagged; the Rs.982 crore order book has no substantial new orders in three months, and US tariffs could slow demand.

rows.label: Order book visibility of Rs.982 crore
rows.why: Unexecuted order book of Rs.982 crore is almost 2x FY26 revenue and management targets at least 2 years of visibility, but no substantial new orders came in over the past three months.

rows.label: International delivery back-ended to Q3 and Q4
rows.why: International revenue fell 12% YoY to Rs.39 crore in Q1 on delivery timing, and management expects three projects to land in Q3 and Q4 (international was about 45% of FY26 revenue).

rows.label: US tariffs could slow US construction demand
rows.why: Management said tariffs could slow US construction demand, though it views the impact on its business as small, and export invoicing carries 60-day credit.

tone.note: Management was confident on the FY27 guidance and the glass unit timeline, but cautious on order inflow and the weak H1; the brief shows analysts pushing on margin dilution from freight and the export margin split, while management asked investors to judge on a yearly basis.

544913|2026-09.headline: H1 FY27 revenue rose 16% to Rs.239 crores and EBITDA rose 22% to Rs.60 crores at a 25.3% margin; FY27 guidance held.
544913|2026-09.overview: H1 FY27 revenue from operations was Rs.239 crores, up 16% YoY, with domestic up 33%, international down 14% on order-execution timing, and fenestration up 82%. EBITDA was Rs.60 crores (25.3% margin, up 138 bps), or 26.9% after stripping out Rs.14 crores of pass-through freight income and expense. Order book stood at Rs.957 crores at September 30, 2026, with management targeting Rs.500 crores-plus of new bookings in Q3-Q4 to hold about 18 months of visibility. Management reiterated FY27 revenue growth of 20-22% and EBITDA margin of 23-25%, and said Q3-Q4 will be stronger.

financial_highlights.change: stated as in the same region as last year
added to both revenue and expenses

segments.name: Domestic (commercial, hospitality, residential, pan-India for Grade A developers)
segments.commentary: H1 FY27 revenue Rs.140 crores, up 33% YoY. Management says Tier 1 demand is strong and the domestic bid pipeline exceeds Rs.3,000 crores. One or two projects are running behind on the client side, which management does not consider material.

segments.name: International (US, Australia and others)
segments.commentary: H1 FY27 revenue Rs.76 crores, down 14% YoY on execution timing. Management says existing US jobs are funded and dispatching daily. New US awards are being held back by developers over tariffs, shipping costs and commodity prices, with a couple of awards expected in Q3-Q4. Israel is a new market, with a first job expected below Rs.50 crores.

segments.name: Fenestration / luxury residential
segments.commentary: H1 FY27 revenue Rs.22 crores, up 82% YoY, which management said reflects project execution rather than a run-rate. Management expects substantial bookings in Q3-Q4 and says the segment carries higher margins.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guided at 20-22%, unchanged from the previous call.
FY27 EBITDA margin guided at 23-25% and PAT margin at 18-20%, both unchanged.
Q3-Q4 expected to be much stronger; an analyst extrapolation of over 30% H2 top-line growth was described as ballpark accurate by management.
Target of Rs.500 crores-plus of new order bookings in Q3-Q4 to end FY27 with about 18 months of visibility.
Glass processing unit commissioning expected July-August 2027, with an estimated 1-1.5% EBITDA margin benefit from Q3-Q4 FY28.
Working capital days guided at around 45 days, with anything below that described as a bonus.
capex_capacity: Glass processing unit project cost is about Rs.70-odd crores, funded from IPO proceeds held separately. Civil construction is expected to finish in 2-3 months, machinery arrival in 6-7 months, and commissioning in 2-3 months.
Other capex is expected to be no more than Rs.20 crores over the next 1.5-2 years, funded from internal accruals.

Current capacity utilisation is about 55-60%. Management says peak revenue of Rs.1,000-plus crores is achievable from the existing facility without material capex, and that this covers about 4 years of 22% growth.
The company has bought a couple of machines and is evaluating additional machinery for BIPV glass production, which is at R&D stage.
demand_pricing: Order book of Rs.957 crores at September 30, 2026, against Rs.846 crores at April 2026 and Rs.383 crores at the start of FY26. Management expects to execute about Rs.350 crores over the next two quarters and says the book will run for 18-24 months.

Average order size is now Rs.60-70 crores, with Rs.80-100 crores jobs described as normal. Bids include a Rs.400 crore Mumbai job, a Rs.450 crore Delhi fenestration quote, and a Rs.225 crore Raidurg bid.
Management says it is choosing jobs on client, terms, margin and execution period rather than chasing win ratio, and that it could win all Rs.3,000 crores of pipeline by cutting prices about 5%.

Q2 wins included a Mumbai hotel job of about Rs.90 crores and two South India data-centre jobs of about Rs.35-40 crores. Management expects data centres to be a few jobs only, with hospitality and commercial as stronger segments.

Pass-through clauses cover aluminium and glass. Claims are certified in 45-60 days, and management says this makes the company risk-free from commodity moves on current projects. Management says none of the jobs are cost-plus; all are re-measurable item-rate contracts.

qa_highlights.question: Are US customers cancelling existing orders, or is the Q3-Q4 strength tied to new orders?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said existing orders are funded and dispatching daily, so none are being stopped. The slowdown relates to new US jobs, which developers are holding until prices normalise. Management expects a pent-up wave of awards after the US midterms or an end to the war.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the sharp Q2 margin increase on flat revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management pointed to Rs.6 crores of escalation claims booked in Q2 for costs incurred in Q1, and to a richer mix from fenestration. It reiterated FY27 guidance of 23-25% EBITDA and 18-20% PAT.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Rs.500 crores order target for Q3-Q4 alone, and what is the split across segments?
qa_highlights.answer: Management confirmed it is for Q3-Q4 only and said bookings will come from all three segments, without giving a split.

qa_highlights.question: How do aluminium and glass price changes flow through?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said pass-through claims are raised after the client-side base rate is reconciled, and are paid 45-60 days after cost is incurred. It said the company carries no commodity risk on current projects.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 20-22% growth guidance net of freight, and what is the freight mechanism?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said guidance is net of freight, which is a pass-through. The CFO said the company receives an advance against freight, so there is no new working-capital blockage.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for Israel and US new-client wins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects a first Israel order in Q3-Q4 FY27, initially below Rs.50 crores, with larger jobs possible within 1.5-2 years. It said the US bids cover both existing and new clients, with a couple of awards possible in the next quarter.

risks_watch: International revenue fell 14% in H1, and Q3-Q4 depends on US and Israel awards that management has not yet booked.
Q2 margin spike was partly due to escalation-claim timing; management itself said margins could move up and down.
H2 revenue depends on converting about Rs.500 crores of bookings in two quarters; no split was given.
Glass processing unit timeline is July-August 2027, and the margin benefit is estimated at 1-1.5%.
Some domestic projects are behind schedule on the client side.
Working capital is currently negative at -19 days, against a stated normalised level of about 45 days.
544913|2026-09.management_tone: Confident and promotional on domestic demand, fenestration and the Q3-Q4 ramp. Noticeably evasive on the US and international order timing, on the Q2 margin spike and on the Rs.500 crores booking split, which management declined to break out.
key_quotes: So, I see no reason to change any sort of guidance for this year and even for the next year.
If I were to drop my prices by 5%, I would get all of the Rs. 3,000 crores orders tomorrow itself.
None of our jobs are cost-plus. All our jobs are re-measurable item rate contracts.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Reported EBITDA margin 25.3% (+138 bps) was lifted by Rs.6 crore escalation claim in Q2; guidance of 23-25% held, and management says margins can move up and down, so H2 margin direction is unclear.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Utilisation is 55-60% and management says Rs.1,000-plus crore peak revenue is achievable from existing facility without material capex; the glass processing unit only commissions around Q2 FY28, outside the 2-4 quarter window.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: FY27 revenue growth guided at 20-22% with H1 at +16% YoY, implying H2 ~30%+ per management, backed by Rs.957 crore order book (up from Rs.846 crore in April 2026) and Rs.500 crore-plus Q3-Q4 bookings target.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation at 55-60% is low, and other capex is capped at about Rs.20 crore over 1.5-2 years, so no major new capex announcement is expected.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: FY27 revenue growth 20-22% and EBITDA margin 23-25% were only reiterated, and the call gives no sign of a raise, with H1 growth at 16% and H2 needing to accelerate.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: H2 needs over 30% growth and Rs.500 crore-plus of bookings with no segment split, US awards are held back by developers, and some domestic projects are behind on client side.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: BIPV glass is still at R&D stage with machines only being evaluated, so no product launch is firmly scheduled in the window.

rows.label: Israel first order
rows.why: Management expects a first Israel job in Q3-Q4 FY27, initially below Rs.50 crore, a small contributor to H2 revenue.

rows.label: US new awards pent-up wave
rows.why: International revenue fell 14% to Rs.76 crore in H1, and developers are holding US awards over tariffs; management expects a couple of awards in Q3-Q4 and a wave after US midterms, but none are booked.

rows.label: Working capital normalises to about 45 days
rows.why: Working capital is at negative 19 days versus guided 45 days, so the current level is a bonus that management does not expect to hold as a trend.

tone.note: Management was confident on domestic demand, fenestration and the Q3-Q4 ramp, but evasive on US and international order timing, the Q2 margin spike from Rs.6 crore escalation claims, and the Rs.500 crore booking split.

544914|2026-06.headline: Steamhouse Q1 FY27 PAT rose 80.25% YoY to INR18.34 crore on 16.7% steam volume growth; EBITDA margin 24.05%.
544914|2026-06.overview: Steamhouse reported record quarterly steam volumes of about 3,05,816 tons, up 16.7% YoY and 11.52% QoQ, with revenue from operations up 13.35% to INR128.62 crore. EBITDA rose 60.08% to INR30.93 crore, lifting margin to 24.05% (up 702 bps), while PAT rose 80.25% to INR18.34 crore. Management attributed the gains to higher volumes, utilisation (41.40% vs 36.06% YoY) and operating leverage, and noted the exit from low-margin coal trading. Gross debt rose to INR359.48 crore from INR281.62 crore at FY26 end, with IPO proceeds earmarked for debt reduction and capacity expansion.

segments.name: Steam generation and distribution (own boilers)
segments.commentary: Own-generated steam was 73.7% of Q1 FY27 revenue. Management said it will be the source of future growth, with waste-to-energy boilers at Vapi supporting realisation.

segments.name: Steam trading (purchased and resold)
segments.commentary: Traded steam was 22.2% of Q1 FY27 revenue. Coal trading has been discontinued as low-margin; two trading agreements (Dahej SEZ, Haldia) are signed and management declined to split margins between generation and trading.

segments.name: Industrial gases / nitrogen
segments.commentary: PSA-based nitrogen plant of 350 Nm3/hr commissioned at Ankleshwar. Management described it as currently small and plans air separation units for LIN/LOX and other gases.

guidance_outlook: Management aims to take utilisation to 60%-65%; newer boilers expected at about 50% in initial months after commissioning.
Steam volume growth of 5%-10% expected at existing locations; company-level 20%-25% volume growth described as 'very comfortably' achievable with new capacity and demand revival.

EBITDA per ton of about INR1,000 expected to be maintained for next few quarters; Q2 seasonally weaker due to monsoon; full-year performance expected to be at par with or better than Q1 run-rate (management said 'we will try' to sustain growth).
Finance costs expected to moderate in FY27 as IPO proceeds repay high-cost borrowings.
Working capital cycle guided at 35-40 days positive.

Capacity to rise from 345 TPH to approx. 705 TPH; four under-construction projects (Jhagadia, Vapi, Nandesari, AMC Pirana) targeted to go live in FY27; Tarapur 60 TPH by Q4 FY28; IPO-funded Dahej, Ankleshwar and Panoli by Q1 FY29.
Una (Himachal Pradesh) 300 TPH EPC project: expected 8%-10% clear margin per ton, pass-through to customers, no capex; agreement not yet signed.
capex_capacity: Installed steam capacity 345 TPH, about 70% contracted; expansion to approx. 705 TPH.
Around INR60 crore further capex needed to complete the four under-construction projects; another INR170 crore planned over 15-18 months for IPO-funded and Tarapur projects.
Ankleshwar nitrogen PSA plant of 350 Nm3/hr commenced; ASU for LIN/LOX under evaluation with build-own-operate partners as an option.
Una EPC: 300 TPH community boiler, project value approx. INR311 crore incl. GST, funded by Himachal Pradesh Bulk Drug Park Infrastructure Ltd; 9% revenue share to be recovered from end customers.
Pipeline network above 60 km across seven industrial areas; management estimates adding pipelines costs 10%-20% of existing infrastructure.
demand_pricing: Management attributed volume growth to revival in chemical and pharma demand after weak FY24-FY26; tyre and food processing (Haldia agreement) added as new segments.
Customer contracts tenor 1-10 years with non-exit clauses; fuel cost pass-through predominantly monthly, some quarterly; newer contracts include minimum guaranteed off-take.
Management claims 25%-35% cost saving versus captive boilers using furnace oil, LDO or natural gas; less beneficial for large coal-fired textile users, which may be at par.
Monsoon disrupts operations because fuel is wet and industrial clusters flood; Q2 seasonally weaker.
Realisation per ton improved due to better utilisation and higher waste-to-energy mix at Vapi.

financial_highlights.metric: Clean EBITDA (adj. for operating lease expenses)

financial_highlights.change: +80.25% YoY (vs INR10.18 crore); PAT margin 14.26%, +529 bps
vs 36.06% in Q1 FY26 and 38.32% in Q4 FY26
vs INR281.62 crore at FY26 end

qa_highlights.question: Is there seasonality in the business across quarters, and what explains the Q1 volume jump over Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is no real consumption seasonality, but monsoon is challenging (wet fuel, flooded industrial clusters). Q1 volume growth was attributed to chemical and pharma demand recovering and repeat customers.

qa_highlights.question: What share of the 345 TPH capacity is contracted, and can customers terminate contracts early?
qa_highlights.answer: About 70% of the 345 TPH installed capacity is tied up under contracts. Tenure ranges 1 to 10 years with non-exit clauses, and management said customers rarely move to captive boilers.

qa_highlights.question: What is the value proposition to win customers from competitors or in-house boilers?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is generally no competitor in most geographies. Claimed cost saving versus captive furnace oil, LDO or natural gas is 25% to 35%, while coal-fired large textile users may be only at par.

qa_highlights.question: What capex is needed to reach 705 TPH and when will projects go live?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR60 crore more for the four under-construction projects, targeted to go live in FY27. Another INR170 crore over 15-18 months for IPO-funded and Tarapur projects; Tarapur 60 TPH by Q4 FY28, Dahej/Ankleshwar/Panoli by Q1 FY29.

qa_highlights.question: Is utilisation of 41% consistent with the planned ramp, and where does the company target it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management targets 60%-65% utilisation; newer boilers are expected to run at about 50% in initial months after commissioning. Some capacity is held back for 2-3 years of new demand.

qa_highlights.question: What are receivable days and CFO to EBITDA ratio, and what are the related-party steam purchases from Sanjoo Dyeing?
qa_highlights.answer: Fortnightly billing with payments typically 7th to 15th day. Operating cash flow was about 1.2 times EBITDA last time, expected to hold or be slightly lower. Steam purchases from Sanjoo Dyeing for the Sachin location continue for at least the next few quarters.

qa_highlights.question: What EBITDA margin is expected on the Una project and what is the revenue-share structure?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects about 8%-10% clear margin per ton, passed through to end consumers, with no capex. The 9% revenue share to Himachal Pradesh Bulk Drug Park Infrastructure Ltd is to be recovered from steam customers. Agreement not yet signed.

qa_highlights.question: What is a sustainable volume growth rate and can company-level 20%-25% volume growth be achieved?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects 5%-10% growth at existing locations, with new capacity adding further. CFO said 20%-25% company-level volume growth is achievable 'very comfortably'.

qa_highlights.question: Is INR1,000 EBITDA per ton sustainable, and what about Q2 seasonality?
qa_highlights.answer: EBITDA per ton of about INR1,000 is expected to hold for the next few quarters, with Q2 an exception due to monsoon. Structural changes cited: coal purchases moved from credit to cash, solar power installed, inventory optimisation. Full-year to be at par or better than Q1.

qa_highlights.question: Why is there government interest in community boilers and are more such opportunities in the pipeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Management linked it to Bulk Drug Park and PM MITRA Park schemes from 2021-22 and a March 2024 CPCB guideline pushing SMEs to common boilers. Gujarat Bulk Drug Park tender is live; PM MITRA and Textile Ministry discussions are ongoing.

qa_highlights.question: Why did steam revenue rise 46% when volume rose 17%?
qa_highlights.answer: Realisation improved from better utilisation and asset leverage, plus higher waste-to-energy usage at Vapi. Growth also came from chemical and pharma recovery and new tyre and food processing (Haldia) customers.

qa_highlights.question: Working capital guidance and cash purchases?
qa_highlights.answer: Working capital cycle guided at 35-40 days positive. Coal was bought on credit until May 2026 and has since moved entirely to cash purchases, which management said lowers fuel cost.

qa_highlights.question: Revenue split between own-generated and traded steam, and margin split by business?
qa_highlights.answer: Own-boiler steam was 73.7% of Q1 revenue and traded steam 22.2%. Management declined to split margins between generation and trading, citing competitive sensitivity.

qa_highlights.question: Is the EBITDA CAGR guidance of 30%-35% going to be beaten?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it will try to maintain the Q1 growth momentum for the full year on both EBITDA and revenue, but said 'We are not saying that we will maintain'.

risks_watch: Utilisation is still 41.40% versus a 60%-65% target; newer boilers ramp only to about 50% in initial months, so margin expansion depends on execution.
Gross debt rose to INR359.48 crore from INR281.62 crore; IPO proceeds are expected to reduce high-cost debt, but the timing and extent of finance-cost moderation need tracking.
Q2 seasonality from monsoon (wet fuel, flooded clusters) is expected to dent EBITDA per ton below INR1,000; watch Q2 FY27 print.
Coal trading exit and undisclosed split of margins between own generation and traded steam (22.2% of revenue) limit visibility into core-segment profitability.
Four under-construction projects (Jhagadia, Vapi, Nandesari, AMC Pirana) must go live in FY27; about INR60 crore capex remains plus INR170 crore for IPO and Tarapur projects.

544918|2026-09.headline: LCC Projects Q2 FY27 revenue rose 34% YoY to Rs 886 crore and EBITDA margin widened to over 15.5%, with order book at Rs 8,154 crore.
544918|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue was Rs 886 crore (up 34% YoY), EBITDA Rs 137 crore (up 46%) and PAT Rs 77 crore (up 58%), with H1 revenue of Rs 1,688 crore and H1 EBITDA margin of 15.2%. The company completed its IPO, raising Rs 258 crore via fresh issue, and net worth rose to Rs 1,276 crore. Working capital days rose to 123 from 99 because trade receivables climbed to Rs 674 crore on end-quarter milestone billing, which management says will be realised largely in Q3. Management guided to a 14-15% EBITDA margin for the full year and revenue growth of about 20%.

segments.commentary: Management says about 80% of revenue comes from water and it will keep water as the core focus. Within water, Jal Jeevan Mission is about 20% of the water-sector book, per management.

segments.name: Other sectors (metro, mining, railway, solar)
segments.commentary: About 20% of revenue per management. Q2 non-water share was higher, which management attributed to rain-hit irrigation and water supply work.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue target of Rs 4,300-4,400 crore, about 20% growth; management expects about 40% of revenue in H1 and 60% in H2.
EBITDA margin to be maintained at 14-15% for the year and beyond; management said there is no margin pressure.
Order book target of about Rs 10,000 crore by March 2027 (2.5x expected revenue); management also cited Rs 6,000 crore of inflows for the year and Rs 3,000 crore expected by March.
Working capital days expected to return to 90-100 days by year-end; significant receivable realisation expected in Q3.
Capex of about Rs 50-60 crore a year; Rs 30 crore spent in H1 and Rs 30 crore planned in H2.
Revenue growth of 20% or more targeted for subsequent years.
capex_capacity: H1 FY27 capex about Rs 30 crore; H2 plan about Rs 30 crore; sustainable run-rate about Rs 50 crore a year, including about Rs 14-15 crore earmarked from IPO proceeds.
Precast factory started in Ahmedabad; on-site precast facilities installed to reduce labour dependence.
Approximately 12,000 labourers on site versus requirement of 10,000-12,000, per management.
demand_pricing: Order book Rs 8,154 crore at 30 September 2026, up from Rs 7,953 crore at 31 March 2026; order book to FY26 revenue 2.21x.

Tenders bid worth about Rs 12,000 crore across Chhattisgarh, Gujarat, Odisha and Uttar Pradesh; a further Rs 15,000-20,000 crore of tenders expected before March.

Private sector work comes from large clients (Adani, Reliance, Tata), with awards based on past performance and negotiation rather than L1 alone; one thermal-power water project for a private client (Adani) has started execution.
Management sees opportunities in inter-river linking (about 30 projects identified; work under way on 4-5), data centre water supply, and nuclear power water needs; no data-centre orders in hand.

qa_highlights.question: What is the revenue and order inflow plan for the year?

qa_highlights.question: Why did receivables rise to Rs 675 crore and when will they be realised?
qa_highlights.answer: Billing is done at month-end after certification, with payment usually in 30-45 days. Milestone billing at end-September led to the spike, and management expects most of it to be realised in October.

qa_highlights.question: How much is the cash balance free to use, and why not repay debt?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the cash is not entirely free: about Rs 290 crore is fixed deposits pledged as margin for bank guarantees, and IPO proceeds are earmarked for objectives to be used from October.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capex plan and are mobilisation advances interest-bearing?
qa_highlights.answer: H1 capex was about Rs 30 crore, with a sustainable run-rate of about Rs 50 crore a year. Mobilisation advance was Rs 29 crore at 30 September, mostly interest-free; management avoids interest-bearing advances.

544921|2026-06.headline: Arcil Q1 FY27 standalone PAT rose 107% to INR143 crores on INR1,066 crores recoveries (up 151%), with acquisitions seasonally light at INR353 crores.

Acquisitions were INR353 crores (Arcil share INR143 crores), about INR150 crores lower than Q1 FY26, consistent with the seasonal pattern where most acquisitions occur in Q4. AUM was INR19,574 crores (up 16% YoY) and borrowings fell sequentially to INR1,100 crores, with management expecting to draw down more in the coming quarters. Consolidated PAT was INR59 crores versus standalone INR143 crores, and management urged investors to assess the company on a standalone and full-year basis.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said an improving economy lets ARCs buy cheaply in stress and resolve at higher rates later; real estate assets stressed four to five years ago are now repaying and redeeming SRs.

qa_highlights.answer: Borrowings are seasonal: lines are drawn mainly at year-end for acquisitions. With a strong pipeline for Q2 and Q3, management expects to draw down more and marginally increase leverage.

qa_highlights.question: Is there AUM guidance for FY27, and why is the retail mix rising?
qa_highlights.answer: No AUM target was given; AUM is expected to rise with acquisitions balanced by equal resolutions, roughly 20-25% of opening AUM resolved each year. Mix reflects asset availability, with no target balance.

qa_highlights.answer: Write-backs are event-based recoveries from legal cases. Management cited about INR288 crores in FY24, INR100 crores in FY25 and INR66 crores in FY26, said Q1 should not be a full-year trend, and said maximum write-offs over the next three years total under INR100 crores.

qa_highlights.question: How sustainable is fee income, given fee income is about 2.4% of AUM annualised versus 1.4% a year ago?
qa_highlights.answer: Management fee nearly doubled YoY and is about 45-50% of total fees. Fee income also depends on collections and resolution, not AUM alone. Management said the momentum should be maintained, and fees are earned only on recoveries, with the legacy book carrying no fee.

Mandatory SR investment is 15%, as low as 2.5% in co-investor deals; own share is 22% of AUM, and Q1 FY27 investment is running at about 40% of acquisitions versus 33% in FY26.

544949|2026-09.headline: Swastika Infra H1 FY27 revenue INR207 crores (+5% YoY), Q2 revenue +42% to INR188 crores; unexecuted order book about INR1,420 crores.

Unexecuted order book is about INR1,420 crores (2.8x FY26 revenue), including a roughly INR600 crore Maharashtra order won in late Q2 with a two-year execution period. Management guided FY27 full-year growth in line with FY26, with H2 seasonally heavier.

Full-year growth expected in line with FY26, with execution visible mainly in Q3 and Q4.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the EBITDA margin increase and is 14% the target?
qa_highlights.answer: Margin was a function of revenue mix, with more commissioning and erection work and final milestone billings. Management expects margins to normalise to around 14% on a full-year basis, without exact quantitative guidance.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Q1 decline and what is the working capital outlook?

qa_highlights.answer: Near term, IPO proceeds should reduce debt over the next two to four quarters. Longer term, the company is rated BBB+ and aims for an A- upgrade, and a shift from bank guarantees to surety bonds is expected to lower funding costs and working capital needs.

qa_highlights.question: What share of the order book is executable in the next 6-12 months and are there delays?

qa_highlights.question: How much of the margin is at risk from cost inflation?

RDSS phase 2 is announced, with tenders expected soon. The company is not currently pursuing SCADA or AMI work, but has quoted a BESS tender.

544959|2026-06.headline: Runwal Enterprises Q1 FY27 revenue fell to Rs 3,400 million (from Rs 4,462 million) on occupation-certificate-based recognition, while pre-sales rose ~5% to Rs 4,835 million.

qa_highlights.answer: Pradumna Kanodia said no specific guidance yet, but a general direction on growth (20-25% pre-sales) will be given while maintaining balance-sheet and margin health.

qa_highlights.answer: Pradumna said debt-to-equity fell from 3.1x to 1.5x and debt is now about Rs 1,900 crore external. Future borrowing will be limited and self-liquidating. qa_highlights.answer: Pradumna said SEBI offered a one-time option to halve offer size for entities already approved, given weak markets; the offer was all primary (about 10-11% dilution), and bankers advised taking it.

544999|2026-09.headline: H1 FY27 revenue of ₹219 crore, with Q2 at ₹183 crore driving the half; management guides H2 "materially better" than H1 but gives no formal guidance.
544999|2026-09.overview: Tonbo Imaging's first analyst call after its recent IPO covered H1/Q2 FY27 results. Revenue from operations was ₹219 crore for H1 (vs ₹77 crore in H1 FY26), with Q1 at ₹36 crore and Q2 at ₹183 crore. Q2 EBITDA was ₹44 crore (24.11% margin) against H1 EBITDA of ₹31.15 crore (14.2%), and Q2 PAT was ₹23.5 crore. Management repeatedly asked investors to judge the business on an annual basis because quarterly revenue recognition is lumpy, and declined to give revenue or margin guidance.

financial_highlights.change: gross profit up ~87% vs ₹40 crore in H1 FY26; margin below 51% in FY26 due to product mix
management referred to this as H2; figure appears to be H1 given context

segments.name: Tactical systems
segments.commentary: Thermal weapon sites, binoculars and monoculars; about 70-80% of business per management. Domestic tactical gross margin ~40-45%; tactical orders convert in 3-6 months. About 250 crore of the 408 crore contracts under negotiation are tactical.

segments.name: Platform systems
segments.commentary: Gimbals, fire control systems, RCWS, seekers and EO for platforms; expected to grow in share over time. Domestic platform gross margin ~45-50%; delivery takes 6-18 months. About 150 crore of the 408 crore under negotiation is platform; most of the 250 crore order book is platform-related.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: About 35% of H1 revenue (65% domestic). Export gross margin ~60-65%. Management said about ₹61.5 crore of Q2 revenue came from the US, which it described as platform subsystems.

segments.name: Directed energy (HPM)
segments.commentary: Still development at TRL 4; ~₹160 crore first-system build cost funded by ₹120 crore loan (sanctioned), ₹25 crore IDEX-ADITI grant and ₹15 crore internal accruals. LOIs for 11 units (5 Indian Navy, 6 European). First deliveries expected FY29-30.

guidance_outlook: No formal revenue or margin guidance; management cited the recent IPO as a restriction.
H2 FY27 revenue expected to be materially higher than H1, supported by the ₹250 crore order book, ₹408 crore under negotiation and a pipeline expected to convert within 2-3 months.
Management expects of the order book converting in FY27 about ₹100-200 crore, with the excess carried into FY28.
EBITDA margin expected to be above H1's 14.2% for the full year on higher revenue, better export mix and operating leverage.
R&D spend for FY27 about ₹30 crore (about ₹25 crore capitalised); HPM project cost ~₹150-160 crore over ~2.5 years.
capex_capacity: Manufacturing is outsourced to certified partners (asset-light model); capital is directed to R&D and IP rather than factories.
Tactical subsystems are kept pre-assembled in inventory, allowing tactical orders received by December to convert to revenue within 3-4 months.
Over 130 R&D engineers; 15+ years of R&D; 100% proprietary IP per management.
Bank cash credit limit raised from ₹30 crore to ₹50 crore post quarter-end with one bank; talks ongoing with the other two banks.
HPM first system capitalisation expected after customer intent is established; about ₹20 crore of employee cost capitalised for HPM over 2.5 years.

Tonbo claims ~65% market share in thermal weapon sites in India (20,000 of ~30,000 deployed); expects share to moderate to ~50% as the market grows.
International near-term tactical opportunity of about 10,000 thermal sites and monoculars.

European export order: first-order production units for a multi-sensor stabilised seeker for a state-owned company; option for up to €13 million on acceptance. Included in the ₹408 crore contracts under negotiation, not in the ₹250 crore order book.
HPM pricing: ~₹200 crore per system quoted to Indian Navy; ~$25 million per unit for international customers.
Competitors named: Bharat Electronics, Tata and Alpha Design in India; Epirus internationally in directed energy.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said the ₹28,000 crore figure is the total Indian addressable base at ~₹200 crore per system for ~140 systems, while the ~$290 million figure corresponds to FY30 expected procurement, which is much smaller.

qa_highlights.question: Who are the competitors in directed energy and how does addressable scale compare with Epirus?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Epirus is the only credible competitor with data; Tonbo aims for 3-5 km range, which Epirus does not offer to most export countries, and says it can compete in the same markets (Japan discussions noted).

qa_highlights.question: How will the ₹250 crore order book convert and what is the FY27 revenue path?

qa_highlights.answer: Mostly OCPP (fast, under 12 months), with some capital procurement in RFI/RFP stage taking 1.5 years for trials.

qa_highlights.answer: H1 R&D of ~₹16 crore, of which ~₹3 crore expensed and rest capitalised; FY27 expected ~₹30 crore, ~₹25 crore capitalised. Blue-sky research is expensed; product development after customer intent is capitalised.

Recent IPO limits guidance; investor reliance on annual rather than quarterly numbers.

545001|2026-09.headline: Q2 FY27 record quarter: revenue up 24.7% to INR373 crore, EBITDA up 36.6% to INR65 crore, with margin rising to 17.6%.
545001|2026-09.overview: Sahajanand Medical Technologies reported its first earnings call as a listed company, with Q2 FY27 setting record revenue, EBITDA and PAT. EBITDA grew faster than revenue on operating leverage in employee and other expenses, though gross margin fell about 170 bps in H1 on traded-product mix and input costs. Reported H1 PAT growth of 7.5% is depressed by a one-off INR8.7 crore tax credit in H1 FY26; excluding it, PAT grew about 39%. Management guided to 150-200 bps annual EBITDA margin expansion and mid-to-high teens constant-currency growth, while H1 free cash flow was slightly negative after capex.

financial_highlights.change: +36.6% YoY; margin 17.6% vs 16% a year ago
+7.5% YoY; about +39% excluding INR8.7 crore one-off tax credit in H1 FY26
vs 76% a year ago (about -170 bps, of which ~150 bps mix)

financial_highlights.metric: H1 free cash flow (after capex and lease payments, before interest)

financial_highlights.change: close to 1x net debt/EBITDA; borrowings INR300 crore, cash and liquid investments INR114 crore
from 138 days in FY26 and about 144 days in FY25

segments.name: Vascular intervention
segments.commentary: 58% of H1 revenue, up 16% YoY; core business including stents, balloons and PTCA catheters.

segments.name: Structural heart
segments.commentary: Grew about 40% in Q2, with TAVI and occluders both up about 40%.

segments.name: Other (largely traded products, incl. IVUS in Europe)
segments.commentary: Fastest-growing category, up 52% in H1; trading now about 25-26% of revenue per analyst question, with management citing IVUS demand tailwind and EBITDA-accretive but gross-margin-dilutive economics.

segments.name: Rest of World
segments.commentary: Grew 37% in H1 and is now the largest region at 40% of revenue.

segments.name: Europe
segments.commentary: Grew a steady 23% in both quarters; 36% of revenue.

segments.name: India
segments.commentary: Growth accelerated from 6% in Q1 to 15% in Q2.

guidance_outlook: Constant-currency revenue growth in the mid-to-high teens; management said mid-teens is a conservative baseline for FY27 and FY28. Currency gains would be over and above this.
EBITDA margin expansion of 150-200 bps per year in FY27, FY28 and FY29, taking margin to about 20% by FY29 from 14.1% in FY26.
Capex of about INR70 crore in FY27 and about INR70 crore in FY28 (INR44 crore spent in H1 FY27), covering vertical integration, automation, maintenance at the Sachin plant and some capacity addition.
Effective tax rate expected at 32-35% for the next two to three years, due to higher-tax geographies (Spain, Brazil, Germany) and loss-making subsidiaries without deferred tax assets.
Working capital days expected to fall by about 15 days over three years, to roughly 100-110 days from about 128 days; inventory is the main lever, receivable days already at 75.
Hydra Elevate already CDSCO-approved; Hydra next-generation valve and AVDC 1.5/TAVI 2.0 launch expected in FY27, possibly as early as Q3 and no later than Q4; PTCA catheters targeted for FY28.
EU MDR: Supraflex Cruz certified; Pipit NC and SC completed audits; Hydra and Cocoon technical files submitted, ahead of the end-2027 transition deadline.
capex_capacity: FY27 and FY28 capex guidance of about INR70 crore per year; INR44 crore spent in H1 FY27. Mix: vertical integration, automation, maintenance at Sachin legacy plant, and a small capacity component.

Management said current capacity suffices for at least 1.5 years, with capex unlikely to rise meaningfully above INR70 crore for the next two to three years. It declined to give peak revenue capacity guidance.

DES utilisation H1 FY27: 79% at Surat and 20% at Telangana (from 64% at Telangana per the analyst's reference). Balloon utilisation: 72% at Surat and 57% at Telangana. New drug-coated balloon line at Surat at 40%.
Surat PTCA utilisation fell to 72% from 97% YoY; management attributed this to inventory optimisation, as previously produced stock was converted to revenue faster than expected.
Gross fixed asset turnover was about 7x before the Telangana plant; management expects it to rise as Telangana ramps up.

Hyderabad (Telangana) technical sterilisation capacity of 9,000 for TAVI in the RHP was not shown in the deck, which shows 3,000 commercial capacity at 60% utilisation. Management said ramp-up of TAVI or occluder capacity is not capex-intensive.
demand_pricing: India: DGHS notification on single-use devices is a tailwind, mainly for PTCA catheters (Pipit SC/NC); implants (stents, TAVI, occluders) cannot be reused. Management does not expect it to lift the 9-10% industry growth to 15-20%.

Europe: TAVI market share about 1.5% (not yet 2%) in low single digits; management expects faster traction once Hydra valve and AVDC are launched. Europe is the largest addressable region for structural heart.
Pricing: broadly stable across all product segments, negotiated hospital by hospital in India, with competitive landscape, product merit and commercial team capability as drivers.

Trading (other products) is rising on IVUS demand after reimbursement in developed markets about two years ago; management said it is gross-margin-dilutive but EBITDA-accretive because SG&A is shared.

International: TAVI not yet approved in Brazil; Australia launched and Canada approved recently. Stents present in more than 70 countries; countries with commercial presence fell to 70 in H1 from 77 in FY26 due to distributor bulk-buying timing, per management.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 and FY28 capex plan and how much has been spent?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR70 crore guided for each of FY27 and FY28, with about INR44 crore spent in H1 FY27, split across vertical integration, automation, Sachin plant maintenance and small capacity additions.

qa_highlights.question: Can gross margin improve via backward integration, and what is steady-state EBITDA margin?
qa_highlights.answer: No gross margin uplift quantified until processes are set up and cycles run; EBITDA margin guided up 150-200 bps a year, reaching about 20% by FY29, driven by European operating leverage with teams already in place.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the tax rate high?
qa_highlights.answer: ETR is around 35% because Spain, Brazil and Germany carry higher tax rates and some subsidiaries are loss-making without deferred tax assets; ETR expected at 32-35% for two to three years.

qa_highlights.question: Why do the RHP and deck show different TAVI capacity figures?
qa_highlights.answer: The RHP included Hyderabad technical sterilisation capacity, not yet commercialised, which the deck excludes; ramping TAVI or occluder capacity needs little capex.

qa_highlights.question: What is the constant-currency growth guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Mid-to-high teens, with mid-teens as the conservative baseline for both the current and next year; reported currency impact cannot be guided.

qa_highlights.question: What is the working capital reduction outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Around 15 days of further improvement over three years, to about 100-110 days from about 128 days, mainly from inventory reduction.

qa_highlights.question: What is the peak revenue potential on current capacity plus INR70 crore annual capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give a peak revenue number, saying TAVI capacity at Hyderabad generates much more revenue per unit of capacity than stents and catheters, so no simple calculation is available.

qa_highlights.question: What is the market share in Europe for TAVI, and how will Europe's structural heart business grow?
qa_highlights.answer: TAVI market share is about 1.5% in Europe; Europe is the largest structural heart market and growth is expected to hold or accelerate with the new Hydra valve and AVDC launch.

qa_highlights.question: Breakdown of trading/others revenue (IVUS, OCT, thrombectomy) and the impact of the Boston Scientific acquisition of thrombectomy business?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give product-level breakdown, citing its no-product-guidance policy; trading growth was attributed to IVUS reimbursement tailwind.

rows.why: Management guides 150-200 bps EBITDA margin expansion each year, taking margin from 14.1% in FY26 to about 20% by FY29; Q2 margin already 17.6% vs 16% a year ago, but H1 gross margin fell ~170 bps to 74.3% on trading mix.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Management says current capacity suffices for at least 1.5 years; Telangana DES utilisation is only 20% and Surat PTCA fell to 72% from 97%, so no new plant is signalled.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Mid-to-high teens constant-currency growth guided with mid-teens as conservative baseline for FY27 and FY28; H1 revenue up 24.9% reported, though constant-currency growth slowed to ~15% in H1.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex held at about INR70 crore per year for FY27 and FY28 (INR44 crore spent in H1 FY27), and management says capex is unlikely to rise meaningfully above that for two to three years; utilisation is low, so no new capex is needed.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Mid-teens constant-currency is called conservative, and currency gains come on top; India growth accelerated from 6% in Q1 to 15% in Q2, but no formal upgrade is given yet.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Gross margin fell ~170 bps in H1, trading mix is rising to about 25-26% of revenue, H1 FCF was -INR1.8 crore, and the Hydra/AVDC launch timing is not yet confirmed.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Hydra next-generation valve and AVDC 1.5/TAVI 2.0 launch guided within FY27, as early as Q3 and no later than Q4; PTCA catheters targeted for FY28.

rows.label: Cash conversion cycle down to 100-110 days
rows.why: Cash conversion cycle at 128 days in H1 FY27, from 138 in FY26; management guides ~15 days further reduction over three years, mainly from inventory, with receivables already at 75 days.

rows.label: EU MDR certifications ahead of end-2027
rows.why: Supraflex Cruz certified and Pipit NC/SC audits completed; Hydra and Cocoon technical files submitted, ahead of the end-2027 transition deadline.

rows.label: Europe TAVI share gain
rows.why: TAVI share in Europe is about 1.5% (not yet 2%) and growing at 23% in both quarters; management expects faster traction after the Hydra valve and AVDC launches, but this is conditional on those launches.

tone.note: Management was confident on growth, margin guidance, and cash conversion, backed by numbers, but was evasive on trading split, peak revenue capacity and gross margin uplift; analysts pushed on the gross margin decline and the trading mix.

545004|2026-09.headline: Jio Platforms Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 11.4% YoY to ₹40,475 Cr, EBITDA up 16.6% to ₹21,879 Cr at a 54.1% margin.
545004|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 was the first quarter reported after listing; management reported 542.4 million customers, 36 million YoY net adds and 9.1 million adds in the quarter, with 5G base at 300 million. Consolidated revenue of ₹40,475 Cr grew 11.4% YoY, EBITDA of ₹21,879 Cr grew 16.6% and margin expanded about 250 bps YoY, with management saying ~78% of incremental revenue flowed to EBITDA. PAT rose 13.7% YoY to ₹8,387 Cr, and EBITDA less capex was ₹15,449 Cr for the quarter (up 52.5% YoY) and ₹32,130 Cr for H1. Management framed growth around four pillars (grow, deepen, convert, build) and pushed a 'digital gateway' model, while explicitly not using tariff hikes as the main ARPU lever. Net leverage was 0.11x at 30 September; the call also covered the IPO (about ₹30,188 Cr of issue proceeds, 24.5x oversubscribed) and international partnership plans.

financial_highlights.change: Net debt positive after IPO proceeds

segments.name: Connectivity (Jio consolidated connectivity entity)
segments.commentary: Revenue ₹35,307 Cr, up 10.8% YoY; EBITDA ₹20,505 Cr, up 14.7% YoY, margin 58.1%.

segments.name: Standalone JPL (digital services and other)
segments.commentary: Standalone revenue up 23% YoY to ₹4,881 Cr, which management said captures the digital services monetisation not in the connectivity ARPU.

segments.name: Home broadband (FWA/UBR)
segments.commentary: Broadband homes reached 30 million, with ~7.3 million YoY net adds; roughly half of the base is fixed wireless access (FWA), and FWA drives most new additions.

segments.name: Mobility (5G)
segments.commentary: 5G customers reached 300 million (66 million YoY adds, 15 million QoQ); Jio holds 51% of wireless broadband subscribers and 60% of the 5G subscriber base.

guidance_outlook: Management said capex peak is behind it and capex for the next four to five years is not expected to exceed last year's level, so free cash flow should grow.
Dividends were not committed; management said growth is the priority and the first year as a listed company will be used to learn before deciding on payouts.
International: management targets 10 to 15 sizeable partners (not niche markets), using a managed-service, asset-light model rather than hardware or SaaS sales; no timing given.
Management said the Gemini offer's initial term is 18 months and it has not yet reached 12 months; no decision yet on charging after expiry.
Tariff increases: management said no decision yet and ARPU is not the only lever; timing will depend on market and macro conditions.
capex_capacity: 5G standalone investment is complete; management said capex for the next four to five years will not exceed FY27-level spend.
UBR (unlicensed broadband radio) home broadband stack has gone through four generations in about three years; management estimates a lead of at least 2.5 to 3 years over the nearest competitor.
Unlicensed UBR cost per user is about $3 against ARPU of about $6, per management, supporting the high-to-low ARPU market strategy.
Management said no incremental spectrum or capex is needed to convert the 4G base to 5G, per the call.
Radisys (already owned) is the existing channel for technology supply to operators, cited as the model for partnerships without direct competition.
demand_pricing: Management sees 340 million new mobility users (240 million from 2G users with other operators, ~100 million from demographic additions over five years).
Fixed broadband penetration is ~20% of ~330 million homes (~64 million connected); management targets ~46% by FY2031 and sees 150 million as a potential fixed broadband opportunity.
Digital economy target of $1.4 trillion cited; 80 million small merchants and 350,000 leased lines are cited as enterprise opportunities.
Digital services: Gemini voice AI usage rose from 2 minutes to over 7 minutes; home subscribers pay about 15% more for 13 OTT apps bundled, per management.
Competition: management said Jio's FWA base is 2x the nearest operator and it expects 5G adds to be driven by 4G-to-5G migration and share gains from other operators.

qa_highlights.question: Go-to-market for digital services, scale expected over 2-3 years, and international partnership timing.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said digital revenue will come from enterprise, home and mobility; partnership talks are two-way, with equal engagement on UBR and full OSS/BSS stack; no timing was given.

qa_highlights.question: Why there is no converged single bill for connectivity and digital services.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is focusing on converged go-to-market and one bill, but said that story is still to play out.

qa_highlights.question: Free cash flow, dividends and capex intensity given the asset-light model.
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said capex has peaked and will not exceed last year's level for four to five years; management said growth is the priority and dividends will be considered after the first listed year.

qa_highlights.question: Tariff hikes and ARPU, given about 2.5 years since last hike.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said tariffs depend on several factors and it will decide at the right time; ARPU rose 3.5% YoY organically, and the focus is digital services realisations.

qa_highlights.question: Conflict of interest in international partnerships, given Jio's own connectivity business.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it will not give technology to domestic players, will avoid competing with partners, and the Radisys model is the reference for partnerships.

qa_highlights.question: AI monetisation (token charges) and Gemini pricing after free period.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the Gemini deal runs 18 months, is not near expiry, and that AI will be offered via the telecom harness to the full base; no token charging decided.

qa_highlights.question: Starlink and satellite competition in India and the US.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said satellite direct-to-device capacity is far lower than terrestrial (about 20 kbps per sq km), that Jio covers 99% of India's homes, and that it plans its own LEO system as a complement.

qa_highlights.question: Financial metrics that management wants to hit over five to seven years.
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give a single number and said it will track market share, deployment, and ARPU uplift; it cited FY26 EBITDA above $8 billion.

risks_watch: ARPU growth relies mainly on mix (+3.5% YoY); no tariff action has been taken in about 2.5 years, and timing is undecided.
Digital services revenue is still small (standalone revenue ₹4,881 Cr); the monetisation case depends on partner (3P) adoption and Gemini economics after the 18-month free term.
International strategy has zero customers and zero revenue; partnerships are not yet signed and no timing was given.
Competition from satellite (Starlink) and other FWA players; management claims a 2.5 to 3 year technology lead, which is not independently verified.
Watch next quarter for: any tariff move, first international partner announcement, converged billing rollout, and dividend policy.
545004|2026-09.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on growth, operating leverage and the IPO; management was firm on 'growth over dividends' and did not commit to tariff timing or international partners, deferring those answers repeatedly.
key_quotes: Growth is definitely life. There is no thinking any which way, otherwise, on dividends, Reliance has always led the way and we will be trying to follow the same things.
We do not want to be dependent on it, at the right time, those can happen.

We want to think maybe 10 to 15 partners that give us sheer scale and again, what I want to highlight to everyone is like you will think this is only for the developing markets, it is not, it is for the developed markets also.
Dan Bailey: the critical thing here is that every one of these telcos is facing the same issues that we have already faced, and we are going there to solve their issues.

rows.why: EBITDA margin rose about 250 bps YoY to 54.1% with ~78% of incremental revenue flowing to EBITDA, and ARPU rose 3.5% YoY to ₹218.8 on mix while capex is peaking.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: 5G standalone investment is complete and management says capex for the next 4-5 years will not exceed FY27-level spend, so no major new capacity build is signalled.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: 9.1M quarterly net adds, 5G base at 300M (15M QoQ adds) and broadband at 30M with ~7.3M YoY adds; management sees 340M new mobility users and fixed broadband penetration rising from ~20% toward ~46% by FY2031.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Management says capex has peaked and will not exceed last year's level for four to five years, with 5G standalone complete and no incremental spectrum needed.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: No numeric revenue or margin guidance was given on the call.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Tariff action is undecided after about 2.5 years without a hike, and ARPU growth of 3.5% relies mainly on mix, so ARPU delivery is not locked in.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Digital services are growing (standalone revenue up 23% YoY to ₹4,881 Cr) and Gemini voice AI usage rose from 2 to over 7 minutes, but no specific launch dates were given.

rows.label: International partnerships (10-15 partners, asset-light)
rows.why: Management targets 10 to 15 sizeable partners with zero customers and zero revenue today, and no partner has been signed or timed.

rows.label: Tariff hike decision
rows.why: About 2.5 years since the last hike; management says no decision yet and timing depends on market and macro conditions.

rows.label: Dividend policy after first listed year
rows.why: Management said growth is the priority and the first listed year is for learning, so no payout is committed in the window.

tone.note: Management was confident on growth, operating leverage and the IPO, and firm on growth over dividends, but deferred answers on tariff timing and international partners; analysts pushed on ARPU, Gemini pricing after the free term, and conflict of interest in partnerships.

545005|2026-09.headline: Paras Healthcare Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 23% YoY to Rs 511 crore, with H1 PAT of Rs 90 crore against Rs 44 crore for full FY26.
545005|2026-09.overview: Consolidated revenue for Q2 FY27 was Rs 511 crore, up 23% YoY and 8.6% QoQ, with H1 revenue of Rs 981 crore (up 25%). Operating EBITDA (excluding other income) rose 47% YoY to Rs 120 crore in Q2, with margin gains attributed mainly to material cost efficiency, formulary compliance and case mix. Group occupancy rose to 76.3% in Q2 from 62.5%, and new hospitals (Srinagar and Ludhiana) moved to positive EBITDA. Working capital absorbed Rs 172 crore in H1, with receivables rising from Rs 350 crore in March to Rs 518 crore, and net debt stands at Rs 620 crore after IPO-funded repayments.

segments.name: Mature hospitals (Gurgaon, Patna, Panchkula, Darbhanga)
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 8.5% in Q2 and 9.1% in H1; Q2 operating EBITDA margin 29.6% (up 360 bps YoY), H1 margin 28.9%; H1 occupancy 76.5%.

segments.name: Emerging hospitals (Ranchi, Jaipur-area unit as named 'Adepur' in transcript)
segments.commentary: Revenue up 27.2% in Q2 and 43.2% in H1; H1 EBITDA margin 18.3% vs 12.4%; H1 occupancy 68.6% vs 49.1%. Ranchi reported 25.8% margin in Q2.

segments.name: New hospitals (Srinagar, Ludhiana as named 'Vlampur' in transcript)
segments.commentary: Revenue up 139% in Q2 and 147% in H1; operating EBITDA turned positive at Rs 15.8 crore in Q2 (vs negative Rs 13 crore in FY26); H1 margin 18.7%; H1 occupancy 68.4% vs 27.8%.

guidance_outlook: No formal revenue guidance given; management said trends can be used for modelling.
Long-term steady-state blended operating margin targeted in the mid-20s range; management said this is a playbook, not guidance.
About 200-250 beds yet to open (Kanpur wings and Ranchi), taking operational beds from ~1,500 toward ~1,800; Kanpur and Ranchi additions expected by end of FY27.
Gurgaon adds ~300 beds (golf course extension) and Ludhiana ~500 beds over the next 12-18 months, per management.
Operating EBITDA margin (excl. other income) expected to stay in the 2.8-3x range... (AOL figure) management expects this trend to continue.
capex_capacity: Capex of about Rs 90 crore in H1 across various units, plus payments for a new Gurugram-area unit (transcript: 'Gulbagh 2').
Dandhi (Darbhanga) has 435 beds; roughly half opened, with two more wings pending.
Kanpur: more beds to be opened by end of FY27; impanelments under insurance and government schemes completed.
Robotic surgery programs running at Gurgaon, Patna, Panchkula and newly launched at Ranchi; liver transplant extended from Gurgaon to Panchkula and Patna.
Management said expansion would be asset-light; acquisitions are low priority given current commitments, though not ruled out.
demand_pricing: Group occupancy 76.3% in Q2 FY27 vs 62.5% YoY; H1 occupancy 73% vs 59%.
Kanpur occupancy rose from 22.7% in H1 FY26 to 78.4% in H1 FY27.
Srinagar occupancy 60.4% in H1 FY27.
Revenue mix H1 FY27: cash/self-pay 32%, insurance 24%, government schemes and PSUs ~44% (as stated in transcript, partly garbled).
Rajasthan state government scheme temporarily suspended across multiple hospitals including Udaipur; company says it has recovered 30-40% of state scheme business there.
Management says payor-mix shift toward cash and insurance is a stated priority, with marketing and tertiary/quaternary programs to drive it.

qa_highlights.question: Why was Udaipur soft in the quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the Rajasthan state government scheme was reviewed and temporarily suspended across multiple hospitals in the state; Udaipur overall business grew in absolute terms and about 30-40% of state scheme business has been recovered.

qa_highlights.question: How has Kanpur ramped up?
qa_highlights.answer: Occupancy rose from 22.7% in H1 FY26 to 78.4% in H1 FY27, driven by new empanelments, more clinicians and a specialty-focused mix; Kanpur insurance and government scheme empanelments are complete.

qa_highlights.question: Why did working capital absorb so much cash despite profit growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the Rs 172 crore outflow to DSO rising from ~79 to ~92 days, from the 25% business growth, faster growth at new hospitals, payor mix and lumpy payments from certain peer groups; it expects normalisation as mix improves.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Rs 50 crore item in other financial assets?
qa_highlights.answer: It is a long-term fixed deposit made from the Rs 80 crore equity infusion in April 2025, reclassified as other financial assets because it is non-current.

qa_highlights.question: Sustainable margin for mature hospitals and how new hospitals should evolve?
qa_highlights.answer: Management described a lifecycle: new hospitals start negative, reach mid-to-high teens, then emerging, then mature at mid-to-high 20s; the blended steady state should be in the mid-20s, though no formal guidance was given.

qa_highlights.question: Will the low AOL-type operating loss per bed continue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the operating loss figure has consistently been in the 2.8-3 range and expects it to continue, helped by case mix (oncology, radiation, robotics, transplants) and occupancy.

qa_highlights.question: Is there headroom to grow occupancy in mature hospitals?
qa_highlights.answer: Patna and Panchkula have further room; Gurgaon is constrained, which is why the golf course extension is planned. Darbhanga remains a feeder to Patna while adding tertiary programs.

qa_highlights.question: How long will emerging hospitals take to reach mature margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said emerging hospitals typically take 4 to 7 years to move to the mature bucket; Ranchi already delivers mid-20s margins and may be reclassified.

risks_watch: Receivables build-up (Rs 518 crore, DSO ~92 days) and its normalisation in H2.
Rajasthan government scheme suspension and its effect on Udaipur and other state-scheme-dependent revenue.
Execution of 200-250 bed openings in Kanpur and Ranchi and the Gurgaon and Ludhiana expansions over the next 12-18 months.
Payor mix: government and PSU share of revenue, and the pace of shift to cash and insurance.
Gross debt of Rs 979 crore and net debt of Rs 620 crore; pro forma debt Rs 143 crore post IPO repayments.
545005|2026-09.management_tone: Confident on operations and margin trajectory, with clear quantified KPIs; cautious and non-committal on forward guidance, repeatedly declining to give numbers. Working capital and state-scheme questions were answered with explanation rather than commitment.
key_quotes: Most of the gains in margin improvement were a result of improvement in material cost, again a result of procurement efficiency, formulary compliances and case mix.
I'm not giving a guidance on that but that is the model playbook which we are looking at.
So the blended every time which we are looking at in the long steady state should be in the mid 20s range.

570004|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 revenue rose about 4% to INR1,800 crore and EBITDA about 7%, but a March raw-material shock cost an estimated INR200-250 crore of sales.
570004|2026-03.overview: Management said Q4 consolidated revenue was about INR1,800 crore versus about INR1,750 crore a year earlier, with Hi-Tech up about 8% and plastics down slightly. Consolidated EBITDA grew about 7% and margin rose to 13.2% from 12.8%, with Hi-Tech margin at 19.8% versus 17.5%. For FY26, revenue grew about 11% and Hi-Tech grew over 20%, while plastics grew only 2.4%. Reported PAT was negative at about INR40 crore due to one-time deferred tax unwinding, a Labour Code charge and non-cash NCD unwinding; management cited adjusted PAT of about INR133 crore. Management says debt repayments due in September and March FY27 are to be met from internal accruals and government receivables, with refinancing and equity as backups.

segments.name: Hi-Tech (drip irrigation, tissue culture, solar agri pumps)
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue up about 8% and EBITDA up about 22%, margin 19.8%. FY26 revenue grew more than 20%. Domestic business grew about 12% and retail about 13%, below the company's 15%-plus target because of March sales loss.

segments.name: Plastics (piping, plastic sheets)
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue slightly down, EBITDA up 3.3%, margin 10.2% versus 9.7%. FY26 revenue grew only 2.4% and EBITDA declined. Overseas plastic sheet business is doing reasonably well.

segments.name: Agro Processing / Food
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue grew about 6% but EBITDA declined. FY26 revenue crossed INR2,000 crore, up 9%, with EBITDA up about 9%. UK food revenue rose from GBP 60 million to GBP 68 million, with cost headwinds. Beverage bottling lines (juice and CSD) started in Q4; about INR27-28 crore revenue was booked by end-March.

guidance_outlook: Management expects FY27 to be better than FY26 on revenue, margins, cash flow and balance sheet, though it called FY27 an uncertain year.
Company plans to be PAT positive (reported) in FY27, with positive EPS targeted from next year.

Management expects standalone operating cash flow to rise from about INR350 crore to INR750-800 crore in FY27, with about INR450 crore of government receivables expected to come down and about INR150 crore of government benefits.
Management expects the second half of Q4 to be better than the first half and July onwards to be better than before, if there is no new price shock.
Management said it would not give numerical guidance because of uncertainty, but said FY28 onwards will be focused on growth funded by internal accruals.
Food business expected to improve in FY27 with the end of UK and US cost and market headwinds, duty-free onion imports under India-USDA rules, and beverage expansion.
capex_capacity: Two beverage bottling lines (one juice, one CSD) started in Q4; about INR140 crore invested over December and March quarters, with no incremental working capital needed per management.
Discussions ongoing for 3 additional beverage lines in FY27, with investment decision expected soon.
Tomato processing plant with a Japanese collaborator expected to start around January 2027, ahead of the tomato season.
Alwar plant near Delhi in Rajasthan is being expanded to grow in North India.
Land sale in Tamil Nadu under MoU, expected to close in the next one to two months, per management.
demand_pricing: Raw material shock: PVC and polyethylene prices rose sharply between 20 February and 25 March 2026, with polymer prices more than 50% higher at peak (polyethylene about 60%) within about 20 days.
By late April-early May, PVC had fallen to about 10% above February levels, while HDPE/LLDPE remained about 40% higher; PVC demand has returned.
Farmers postponed purchases in March and April due to price uncertainty and lower prices for farm produce as exports fell.
Management attributes an INR200-250 crore shortfall in Q4 revenue to the March pricing shock; standalone Q4 revenue was about INR1,000 crore versus a potential INR1,250 crore-plus.

Drip irrigation sales FY26: Maharashtra about INR700 crore, South about INR400 crore, West about INR250 crore, North about INR88 crore (up from INR75 crore), East about INR107 crore (up from INR60 crore).

qa_highlights.question: How will the company service its debt given weak standalone cash flow, and what restructuring or fundraise is planned?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said standalone operating cash flow should rise from about INR350 crore to INR750-800 crore, with about INR150 crore of government benefits also available. Backup options include refinancing and equity, with more clarity expected by July. Management said a smaller amount is due in September and most in March FY27, and that about 98% of old interest-bearing term debt was repaid by March.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Tamil Nadu asset sale close to closing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said an MoU is signed for the Tamil Nadu land and it should close over the next couple of weeks to a month, after recent state elections.

qa_highlights.question: When will PAT turn positive, and what is the adjusted PAT?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the FY27 plan is reported PAT positive. Reported FY26 PAT was minus INR40 crore due to one-time items and non-cash NCD unwinding; adjusted PAT was about INR133 crore versus INR97 crore earlier.

qa_highlights.question: What are the bottling plant and UK food business progress and investment?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR140 crore has been invested in bottling over two quarters; first line is operating and about INR27-28 crore revenue was booked by end-March. UK food revenue grew to GBP 68 million from GBP 60 million, with cost headwinds expected to ease in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Is there an IPO plan for the food division?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is some distance away because of market conditions, and is unlikely in the first half of FY27, subject to merchant banker advice.

qa_highlights.question: Why was Q4 revenue short of expectations (about INR200-250 crore), and by segment where?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the shortfall entirely to the March pricing shock and lost farmer demand. It said standalone EBITDA would have been about INR25 crore higher had the sales been realised, and that margins were held.

risks_watch: Debt repayments due in September and a larger amount in March FY27 depend on collection of government and project receivables, and refinancing or equity is the backup.
Polymer prices (HDPE/LLDPE still about 40% higher) and the risk of another price shock affecting Q1 and H1 FY27 demand.
Reported PAT remains negative; the FY27 PAT-positive target depends on cash-based earnings and non-cash items.
Exports fell about 10% in FY26 to INR455 crore; tariffs, shipping constraints and geopolitical risk remain.
UK and US food business cost and market headwinds, and the timing of new beverage lines and tomato plant start.
