So the entire reduction, about INR200 crores, INR250 crores is linked to this pricing shock in March.
And we feel that company would be able to generate adequate internal accruals to be able to take care of that matter.
For FY '27, right, our plan right now is to be PAT positive.

570004|2026-09.headline: Jain Irrigation Q2 FY27 revenue rose over 10% to about INR 1,576 crore, EBITDA INR 207 crore, working capital cycle cut to 179 days.

Adjusted PAT after the NCD wind-down adjustment was about INR 40 crore. Cash conversion was strong, with about INR 206 crore of EBITDA converted to cash, which funded INR 230 crore of NCD repayments. Management said the drought in west and south India and high polymer prices weigh on the next six months, and guided only to flattish H2 volume.

qa_highlights.question: Will margins hold when polymer prices fall?
qa_highlights.answer: Pricing uses average inventory cost, so no negative margin impact is expected on falling prices; fixed-cost absorption could add 1%-2% margin.

590003|2026-03.headline: KVB posted record FY26 net profit of INR2,500 crores (+29%) and Q4 NIM of 4.25%, but guides FY27 NIM down to 3.75-3.8% and ROA to 1.7-1.8%.
590003|2026-03.overview: Karur Vysya Bank reported record quarterly net profit of INR725 crores and full-year profit of INR2,500 crores (+29%), with full-year NIM of 3.97% above guidance. Total business grew 15% to INR2,14,420 crores, with advances up 17% to INR98,754 crores and deposits up 13% to INR1,15,666 crores, though advances growth moderated in Q4 by conscious choice. Management flagged a shift toward preserving relationships over margins: FY27 credit growth is guided at 1-2% above industry, NIM at 3.75-3.8%, and ROA at 1.7-1.8%. Asset quality stayed stable with GNPA at 0.75% and a one-time INR163 crore prudential provision taken against geopolitically exposed sectors.

Includes INR163 crore one-time prudential provision

segments.commentary: Commercial book grew 11.56% YoY but was flat in Q4; corporate grew 12% YoY, or 20% including credit substitutes (incremental INR969 crores). Growth focused on CRE, capital markets and EPC contractors.

FY27 ROA guided at 1.7-1.8%; credit cost guided at below 1%.
GNPA below 1.5%, net NPA below 1%, slippages below 1% of the asset book, cost-to-income below 50%, LCR maintained at 115-120%.

Branch expansion of 50 branches in FY27 (38 regular, 7 lite, 5 to be shortlisted), front-loaded into H1. Investment yield enhancement of 15-20 bps via HTM rebalancing; duration to be kept around 4-4.5 years over the medium term.

Management sees no need to raise capital in FY27; profit ploughback to fund growth. Dividend declared at 130%, subject to shareholder approval, with the payout on a larger base after the 1:5 bonus issued last year.

Loan-against-mutual-fund IT integration is at final stage, expected launch in H1 FY27; premium credit cards planned in FY27.
Digital: 98% of transactions digital; DLite app rated 4.8 on Google Play and 4.6 on Apple App Store, with 2.5 million monthly active users.
demand_pricing: Retail term deposit rates raised in April 2026; new products at 7.2%, with blended incremental cost seen at 7.2-7.5% as senior citizen deposits are 27-30% of total deposits.

Gold loans: jewel loans are 30% of the book against an internal cap of 35%; agri gold yields are about 10.75-11%, and management plans to cut pricing toward 9.5-9% to limit growth.
Working capital utilisation fell 2-3% across sectors in Q4, as customers ran down lines amid geopolitical uncertainty; textile is flagged as the most exposed sector.

qa_highlights.question: What is FY27 NIM guidance versus the FY26 beat?

qa_highlights.question: What drives the competitive pressure on yields?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said concession pricing has moved and the bank has held rates, but it now must cut to retain good accounts. Retaining accounts is a priority over margins; Q4 yield benefit of 16 bps came from repricing of 25-30% of the book.

qa_highlights.question: What sectors received the INR163 crore prudential provision?

qa_highlights.question: Will the ECL transition and steady-state credit cost be quantified?

qa_highlights.question: Why is FY27 credit growth guided lower than FY26?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the bank chose a prudent, moderated approach in a benign-but-volatile environment to avoid credit cost offsetting yield gains, with capital not the binding constraint.

qa_highlights.question: What is the gold loan LTV and outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said gold loans are capped at 75% LTV for retail and 80-85% for agri, with margin of 20-40%; loans above 75% LTV are under 1-1.5% of the portfolio.

rows.why: 50 branches planned in FY27 (38 regular, 7 lite, 5 to be shortlisted), front-loaded into H1 with a firm plan behind it.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Credit growth guided at only 1-2% above industry vs 18% in FY26, and Q4 advances growth moderated by choice; working capital utilisation fell 2-3% across sectors, though retail (+25% YoY) and deposits (+13%) provide some support.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: CRAR at 18.76% and management says capital is not a constraint and no capital raise is needed in FY27; utilisation read is not a capacity constraint, and no new capex was flagged beyond branches.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: FY27 guidance was cut on NIM (3.75-3.8% vs 3.97%) and credit growth moderated; management is guiding conservatively and trading margin for relationships.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Retail term deposit repricing impact to be seen in Q1 FY27, competition forcing rate cuts to retain accounts, ECL transition not yet quantified, and wage provision from November 2026 not yet booked.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Loan-against-mutual-fund integration at final stage with launch expected in H1 FY27, and premium credit cards planned in FY27.

rows.label: Yield concessions and gold loan repricing
rows.why: Management says it must cut rates to existing and new borrowers to retain accounts, and plans to cut agri gold yields from about 10.75-11% toward 9.5-9%.

rows.label: Retail term deposit renewals and cost of funds
rows.why: Retail term deposit renewals are 70-75% and senior citizen deposits are 27-30% of total, with new product rates at 7.2% and blended incremental cost seen at 7.2-7.5%, which may push up cost of funds.

rows.label: Corporate BBB-book push for RWA density
rows.why: Management is leaning into BBB-rated corporate accounts with gating conditions to lift RWA density, while acknowledging fierce competition for AAA/AA names; corporate grew 12% YoY (20% incl. credit substitutes).

tone.note: Management was confident on the record FY26 profit and branch expansion, but cautious and defensive on FY27 margins and growth, openly trading NIM for relationships; analysts pressed on NIM, yield competition and the ECL and wage provisions, which management deferred.

590003|2026-06.headline: KVB Q1 FY27 net profit rose 45% YoY to INR756 crore, but NIM of 4.26% and sequentially lower write-off recoveries (INR103 crore vs INR216 crore) weigh on the outlook.
590003|2026-06.overview: Karur Vysya Bank reported Q1 FY27 net profit of INR756 crore, up 4% QoQ and 45% YoY, with NIM of 4.26% and ROA of 2.11%. Total business grew 16% YoY to INR2,27,267 crore, with advances and deposits each up 6% QoQ. Sequentially, operating profit fell 12% to INR1,096 crore and non-interest income fell 28% to INR442 crore, mainly on lower write-off recoveries and one-offs. Management kept the full-year NIM guidance of 3.7% to 3.8% but said NIM should be above 4% next quarter, and it will review full-year guidance at end-September.

financial_highlights.value: Not stated in INR; growth 32% YoY, 5% QoQ
financial_highlights.change: Highest growth in 5 years per management
+41 crore QoQ (about 6%), including AS 15 retiral cost up INR47 crore
+1 bp QoQ; 4.34% incl. 8 bp one-off interest recovery
Includes INR68 crore NPA and INR22 crore standard asset provisions
Lower from INR187 crore in Q4
Down from INR216 crore in Q4 (-INR113 crore)
Management expects 42.5% to 43% as a likely near-term level

segments.name: Retail (RAM, 86% of advances)
segments.commentary: Retail advances grew 6% QoQ and 23% YoY, led by jewel loans (+12% QoQ) and mortgages (+9% QoQ). BNPL book grew 2% QoQ, with management saying the Axio partner was restructuring after Amazon took full ownership.

segments.name: Agriculture
segments.commentary: Agri portfolio grew 5% QoQ; agri jewel loans are 92% of agri book. Gold LTV is 63.7% for agri and 56.83% for non-agri.

segments.name: Commercial banking / SBG & BBG (part of 14% corporate balance)
segments.commentary: Commercial segment grew 6% QoQ, with business banking disbursements up 45% QoQ. Management said Q4 FY26 flat growth was an aberration and expects ~18% growth for the year.

segments.name: Corporate and institutional (14% of advances)
segments.commentary: Grew 6% QoQ on CRE, capital market participants and EPC/infrastructure; disbursements are at a 5-quarter high. Credit substitutes rose INR171 crore.

segments.name: Deposits / CASA
segments.commentary: Deposits grew 6% QoQ; CASA grew 9% QoQ, with current accounts up INR1,753 crore (+19%) and savings up INR901 crore (+4%). Retail households are 72% of deposits.

guidance_outlook: Full-year NIM guidance of 3.7% to 3.8% kept; management expects NIM at 4%+ next quarter, with full-year guidance to be reviewed at end-September.
Credit growth guided at 1% to 2% above industry growth for the rest of the year; management said it would be 1% above industry in RAM if system grows, and more cautious in corporate.
GNPA expected below 1.5%, net NPA below 1%, and slippages below 1% of loan book for the year.
Credit cost guidance of about 1% is seen as conservative; management said it could be much lower. Yield on advances expected to fall 10 bp next quarter, and cost of deposits to rise 5 to 10 bp.
Yield on investments targeted at about 7% by exit of FY27 (6.83% in Q1). Write-off recovery target of INR500 to 600 crore per year, though quarterly recoveries will be lumpy.
Cost-to-income expected to rise to 42.5% to 43% (from 41.74%) as about 50 branches are opened in H1 FY27 (25 by end-Q1 per management). Opex impact estimated at 0.5% to 1%.
capex_capacity: Opened 2 branches in Q1 FY27; target of 50 branches in H1 FY27, with 25 to be completed by end-June and the rest by end of H1.
Mortgage-focused branches raised from 144 to 175 this year. Small business group relationship model extended to 77 branches from 75.
Staff strength rose from about 7,000 to 9,500 over the past year; management expects more manpower to be added this year.
Loan against mutual funds product to launch by end-Q2 FY27; credit card relaunched for existing customers, with new-to-bank rollout planned in H2 FY27.
demand_pricing: Competition and customer retention are compressing yields; management said some customers want up to 0.5% concession and that it may cede accounts or lower yields.
Housing: bank is slowing growth because public sector banks are pricing at 7.5% to 8.5%. It had INR160 crore of housing disbursements where yields were above 8.25% to 8.5%.
Fixed-rate book rose from 29% to 34% of advances; MCLR-linked book fell from 14% to 9%; EBLR-linked book stayed at 55%.
Gold loans: average blended yield is about 11% to 12%, with agri PSL benefit possibly taking it to 11.25%. Gold loans are about 30% of advances, against an internal ceiling of 30% to 35%.

Deposit pricing: time deposit rates were raised 40 bp during the quarter to fund front-loaded advances. FCNR(B) pricing is at about 7%, targeting tickets below USD1 million; base is about USD130 million.
Textiles are about 5% of the portfolio and seen as the main war-related risk. Working capital utilisation is steady at 77% to 80%. Management said the bank has not seen SMA build-up as a result.

qa_highlights.question: Will credit growth stay 100-200 bp above system if system growth has moved to around 18%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it will stay about 1% above RAM system growth, but will be more cautious in corporate to avoid repeating the earlier mistake. Corporate is now 14% of advances, down from 45%.

qa_highlights.question: Why did SME YoY growth slow to 12-13%?
qa_highlights.answer: Q4 FY26 was flat because the bank avoided pricing competition and some weak accounts. Q1 growth recovered to 6% QoQ, with commercial disbursements up 45% YoY on NTB plus ETB. Management expects about 18% growth for the year.

qa_highlights.question: What is the ECLGS disbursement and pipeline?
qa_highlights.answer: In commercial, 2,232 applications were received on JanSamarth. INR140 crore disbursed, with INR10 crore in Q1. In corporate, 54 applied and INR80 crore disbursed, with 176 units eligible, of which about 100 may qualify.

qa_highlights.question: What is the gold loan blended yield?
qa_highlights.answer: Management estimated a blended 11% to 12%, with agri PSL benefits possibly pushing it to 11.25%.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the bank pushing a higher fixed-rate book if costs are rising?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said fixed-rate loans at 11% to 15% insulate yields if rates fall later, and 20 to 30 bp of cost increase is manageable.

qa_highlights.question: How should investors think about full-year NIM given the Q2 guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q2 NIM should be 4%+ but full-year guidance of 3.7% to 3.8% is not changed and will be reviewed at end-September. Downside is limited, though a fall to 3.6% to 3.5% would be a concern.

qa_highlights.question: How will the normalisation of write-off recoveries affect ROA over the next 2 to 3 years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said lower write-offs could cut ROA by about 25 bp, not 40-45 bp. Offsets: non-fund income (TPP and guarantees), and 10-15 bp from CASA cost and 10 bp from other income.

risks_watch: Write-off recoveries are lumpy and fell to INR103 crore; full-year target of INR500 to 600 crore is at risk if recoveries stay subdued.
Competition and retention pressure: yield on advances expected to fall 10 bp next quarter, and cost of deposits to rise 5 to 10 bp.
Credit cost and ECL transition: management said the ECL impact is premature to quantify; a normalised credit cost will be indicated in about 10 to 11 months.
SMA-30 rose from 0.17% to 0.22%; slippage ratio is guided below 1%. Textile (about 5% of book), ceramics, logistics and the El Nino/monsoon delay are the main sector watch items.
Gold price declines and El Nino could affect agri gold loans (92% of agri book); management said LTV is 63.7% for agri and 56.83% for non-agri.
key_quotes: I am pleased to report that we could successfully navigate the quarter and maintain our net interest margin at 4.26 .

So that way, if we are going to move to 3.6% and 3.5%, that's a cause of concern. But we are not on the trajectory, and we are trying our level best to manage the portfolio, product mix, all these things and all.
it will be premature at this stage to indicate any normalized credit cost under the new region.
YTD growth, this first quarter growth should not be considered as an indicator for the full year growth at the same tempo.

It was also guarded on deposit costs, corporate growth, and ECL, where it declined to quantify a normalised credit cost.

590003|2026-09.headline: KVB Q2 FY27: net profit INR788 crores (+37% YoY), NIM held at 4.26%, credit cost 0.43%, and advances growth guided to 18-20% for FY27.
590003|2026-09.overview: Karur Vysya Bank reported a strong Q2 FY27 with net profit of INR788 crores, up 4% QoQ and 37% YoY, and operating profit of INR1,162 crores (+14% YoY, +6% QoQ). Total business reached INR2,39,712 crores (+5% QoQ, +18% YoY), with advances up 7% QoQ to INR1,11,589 crores and deposits up 5% QoQ to INR1,28,123 crores. Management guided to 18-20% credit growth, NIM of 4% plus, ROA of about 2% and GNPA below 1.5% for FY27, while flagging that funding costs and loan-yield competition may pressure margins in coming quarters. Management also said the write-off recovery contribution has fallen sharply, and that the bank will rely more on core earnings.

financial_highlights.change: +INR1 crore QoQ; AS-15 provisions lower by INR28 crores

financial_highlights.value: 0.43% annualised (INR94 crores NPA/standard/restructured + INR25 crores floating provision)

segments.name: Retail advances
segments.commentary: Grew 5% QoQ led by mortgages (+12% QoQ) and personal loans (+11% QoQ); retail jewel loans fell 1% to a total jewel book of INR32,153 crores (29% of advances), with LTV of 67% for agri gold and 59% for non-agri gold.

segments.name: Corporate and institutional
segments.commentary: Portfolio grew 12% QoQ (14% of advances), with average ticket size of INR42 crores; credit substitutes grew about INR500 crores in the quarter.

segments.name: Commercial business (SBG and BBG)
segments.commentary: Grew 8% QoQ, with disbursements up about 24% QoQ; tailor-made products (GST surrogate, open term loan) crossed INR450 crores outstanding.

segments.name: Deposits and CASA
segments.commentary: Deposits up 5% QoQ; CASA rose INR1,489 crores in Q2 (current accounts +INR592 crores, savings +INR897 crores); retail term deposits 73% of total deposits, growing 6% QoQ (+INR3,902 crores).

segments.name: Agriculture
segments.commentary: Agri loans grew 4% QoQ; agri jewel loans are 92% of the agri book.

guidance_outlook: Advances growth guided at 18-20% for FY27 (YTD 13%); management cautioned that YTD growth is not an indicator for full-year growth.
NIM for FY27 guided at 4% plus; management said it expects to cross 4% for the next 2 quarters but would not commit to 4.26% being retained.
ROA for FY27 guided at about 2%, with 2.1% reported for Q2.
GNPA guided below 1.5%, NNPA below 1%, slippages below 1%; cost-to-income expected below 45% over the next 2 quarters.
Branch expansion: 50 branches planned for FY27, with 26 to be opened by end-December 2026 and the balance by year-end.
Liquidity coverage ratio to be maintained in the 115-120% range versus 129% reported.
capex_capacity: 20 branches opened in H1 FY27 (including 2 in Q1); 50 planned for FY27.
Branch expansion focus: South India first, then Maharashtra and Gujarat, then Central and North, and East last.
Working capital utilisation steady at 76-79% over 1-1.5 years; US-export textile borrowers at about 55-56% utilisation.
Management sees little customer capex or textile modernisation demand currently.
demand_pricing: Credit demand in corporate and institutional segment came from EPC, infrastructure, commercial real estate, capital market participants and selective textile and NBFC capex.
Textile portfolio is about 5% of advances; split is 40% upstream (spinning/ginning), 22% midstream, 38% downstream (finished goods and apparel), with downstream most exposed to US tariffs.
Bank is seeing poaching in mortgages from banks offering lower rates; management chose not to match and accepted some account losses, while housing loans were also de-emphasised.
Vehicle loans trending down as a tactical choice: higher delinquency, 150% risk weight, and funding tightness; funds redirected to gold and mortgages.

Management expects pricing competition from banks flush with FCNR-driven liquidity, which may bring down yields; EBLR book rose to 57% of advances from 55%, fixed-rate book 34%, MCLR book fell to 7% from 9%.
Yield on investments fell 4 bps to 6.79%.

qa_highlights.question: Is there any stress in gold loans given rising gold loan NPAs seen in bureau data for some peers?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it has not seen stress on the ground. It tightened margin-call monitoring over the last 1.5 years via a digitised system with a centralised cell, and says auctions are few because customers bring family ornaments and top up or repay. Retail gold is priced at about 14%, agri gold at 10.75%.

qa_highlights.question: How much bancassurance income is at risk from the proposed IRDA commission changes, and how will it be recouped?
qa_highlights.answer: Management estimated commissions could fall 60-70% in some cases. It said LI penetration of about 1.6% would need to rise to 3.8-3.9% to make up the lost income, implying roughly 50% recoupment needed, and it is reworking product mix and penetration, which ranges from 0.9% to 2.2-2.3% across geographies.

qa_highlights.question: How resilient are non-core income sources (treasury and write-off recoveries) to ROA?
qa_highlights.answer: Treasury contributed 0.06% of the Dupont in both Q1 and Q2. Write-off recovery fell to 0.21% of Dupont from 0.65-0.9% earlier. Management said ROA would still be around 2% if recoveries fall another 10 bps, and that the bank has a pool of about INR2,500 crores of assets to recover from.

qa_highlights.question: What is the total stock of floating and contingency provisions, and what is the split?
qa_highlights.answer: Total provisions are 1.65% of advances including standard and floating; excluding them it is about 1.0-1.04%. Floating provision is INR100 crores (ECL-related, two years ago) plus INR25 crores added this quarter, on top of standard and restructured provisions. Restructured-book provision cover is 40.1%.

qa_highlights.question: Is the corporate and SME demand driven by working capital drawdown or capex, and what is the textile utilisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said working capital utilisation is steady at 76-79% over 1-1.5 years. US-export textile borrowers are at 55-56% utilisation, and capex demand is limited. Textile is about 5% of advances, split 40% upstream, 22% midstream and 38% downstream. Growth comes from takeovers and fresh acquisitions.

qa_highlights.question: Why did RWA rise and what is driving the vehicle loan decline?
qa_highlights.answer: RWA density moved to 58% from a 65% target, driven by selective NBFC exposure (150% risk weight if the bank is not in the rating), corporate growth, consumer credit (125% risk weight), and unhedged FX provisions. Vehicle loans are declining as a tactical call due to fixed rates, dealer commissions, high delinquency, 150% risk weight and deposit tightness; funds moved to gold and mortgages.

qa_highlights.question: Will margins trend down from 4.26%, and what is the repricing outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management would not commit to retaining 4.26%. It expects 4%+ for the next 2 quarters, citing gold loan repricing from MCLR to fixed now complete, corporate yields of 9%+, and possible 3-6 month pricing pressure. EBLR book is about 56-57%, with working capital repricing 25 bps immediately.

risks_watch: Funding cost pressure: management expects deposit rates to stay up for 2-3 months; cost of deposits rose 4 bps QoQ, and a 25 bps repo hike was announced.

NIM sustainability: management would not commit to retaining 4.26% and expects pricing pressure from banks flush with FCNR liquidity over the next 3-6 months, with some accounts possibly repriced lower.
Mortgage and gold loan competition: mortgage poaching at lower rates, and some account losses as the bank declined to match; LTV and margin-call monitoring on gold loans.
Non-core income dependence: write-off recoveries fell to 0.21% of Dupont from 0.65-0.9%, and treasury contributed 0.06%; ROA guidance depends on core earnings.

Regulatory: pending IRDA bancassurance commission changes could cut income 60-70% in some cases; ECL transition timing still being assessed (about 1-1.5 months more clarity), with a 1.65% provision cover.
Leadership: CEO succession search committee formed; the current MD's tenure is under two years.
key_quotes: I am pleased to report that we were able to maintain our net interest margin at 4.26% for this quarter also.
So 4.26% retention that I cannot say anything on that. So -- but 4% and above, I can assure.
As a word of caution, YTD growth should not be construed and considered as an indicator for the full year growth.
So, we feel that we will be below 45% in the next 2 quarters to come.
590003|2026-09.management_tone: Confident on asset quality and ROA, but cautious and hedged on margins and pricing: management repeatedly said visibility is only 3-6 months and would not commit to holding 4.26% NIM. It was evasive on the ECL transition and on the bancassurance impact, which it called fluid.

rows.why: NIM is 4.26% (4.34% incl. 8 bps one-off recovery) but management would not commit to holding it, guiding only 4%+ for the next 2 quarters amid pricing pressure.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.when: 26 branches by end-Dec 2026; balance of 50 by Q4 FY27
rows.why: 20 branches already opened in H1 FY27 and 50 planned for FY27, with 26 more committed for end-December 2026 and the rest by year-end.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Advances grew 7% QoQ to INR1,11,589 crores and 18-20% FY27 growth is guided with YTD at 13%, so the bank needs roughly 5-7% QoQ growth in H2.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Branch rollout is already committed, and working capital utilisation is flat at 76-79%, so no new capex programme is signalled.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: YTD advances growth is only 13% against 18-20% FY27 guidance, and management cautioned that YTD growth is not an indicator for the full year.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Management flagged 3-6 months of pricing pressure from FCNR-flush banks, deposit rates staying up for 2-3 months after a 25 bps repo hike, and ROA would hold near 2% only if recoveries fall another 10 bps.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Tailor-made commercial products (GST surrogate, open term loan) already past INR450 crores, but no new launch was discussed.

rows.label: IRDA bancassurance commission changes
rows.why: Commissions could fall 60-70% in some cases, and LI penetration of about 1.6% would need to reach 3.8-3.9% to recoup roughly 50% of the lost income.

rows.label: Write-off recovery normalisation
rows.why: Write-off recovery fell to 0.21% of Dupont from 0.65-0.9%, so ROA depends more on core earnings, though management says ROA stays near 2% even if recoveries fall another 10 bps.

rows.label: Cost-to-income below 45%
rows.why: Opex was INR770 crores with PPOP at INR1,162 crores, and management expects cost-to-income below 45% over the next 2 quarters.

tone.note: Management was confident on asset quality (GNPA 0.69%, slippages 0.44%) and ROA about 2%, but cautious on margins and would not commit to holding 4.26% NIM; analysts probed gold loan stress, bancassurance income at risk, and the non-core recovery dependence.

590013|2026-03.headline: Xpro Q4 FY26 revenue fell to INR134.37 crore (vs INR158.2 crore) while PBT rose to INR16 crore; FY26 PBT fell to INR41 crore on forex loss and pre-operating costs.
590013|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue from operations was INR134.37 crore against INR158.2 crore a year earlier, while quarterly PBT rose to INR16 crore from INR11.5 crore. Full-year net revenue fell 5.6% to INR505.5 crore and production fell 5% to 31,335 MT, driven by lower Coex (refrigerator sheet and liner) volumes. Full-year PBT fell to INR41 crore from INR58 crore, hit by competitive pricing, input cost volatility, a forex loss of INR11 crore (INR11.14 crore unrealised) and pre-operating costs. The new Barjora dielectric film line entered commercial production on 27 March 2026, and management said polymer prices are rising steeply after the West Asia crisis.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR158.2 crore in Q4 FY25 (down about 15%)
vs INR11.5 crore in Q4 FY25
vs INR39.3 crore in Q4 FY25, broadly flat
down 5.6% from INR535.28 crore in FY25

financial_highlights.value: INR11 crore, of which INR11.14 crore unrealised
financial_highlights.change: vs gain of INR1.49 crore in FY25

segments.name: Biax (dielectric films)
segments.commentary: Biax turnover was about INR140-142 crore for the year, broadly flat because operating capacity was largely unchanged; Q4 Biax sales were INR39 crore. Volumes were capped by available capacity, not demand.

segments.name: Coex (coextruded sheets and refrigerator liners)
segments.commentary: Coex turnover declined on a temporary slowdown in refrigerator production, partly attributed to early monsoon, plus softer raw material prices. Management said Coex volumes are directly correlated with consumer end-market conditions.

guidance_outlook: No revenue or margin guidance given for FY27; management said guidance will be shared publicly when provided.
Barjora new line: target at least 50% utilisation in FY27, 'if not more'; management said two India lines should be in full production in FY28.

UAE (Ras Al Khaimah) subsidiary: trial production expected August-September 2026; commercial operations targeted by Q3 FY27 barring unforeseen circumstances; UAE line expected above 50% utilisation in FY28.
Full capacity utilisation for the India lines expected next year (FY27), subject to West Asia and polymer uncertainty.
FY27 capitalisation: RAK plant is the largest chunk, with modest routine Coex capex; no further new line expected to be capitalised in FY27.
Girish Behal to become Managing Director from 1 January 2027, subject to shareholder approval.
capex_capacity: Barjora dielectric film line entered commercial production on 27 March 2026; about INR240 crore capitalised so far.

RAK (UAE) plant: most key equipment on site and in advanced implementation; not yet capitalised as it is work in process until commercial production is declared; next line to be capitalised around mid-2026.
Subsidiary absorbed a total loss of AED 4.52 million, of which AED 1.95 million was forex movement; USD 9 million fresh equity received from a UAE participant.
Coex capacity at Ranjangaon and Greater Noida: multiple lines; capex there is modest and routine.
INR74.63 crore of preferential and QIP proceeds held in bank pending deployment.
demand_pricing: Dielectric film demand described as structural (electrification, renewables, grid, EV, traction); the company targets ultrathin, hazy and semi-rough films for power capacitors, EV and railway uses.

Polymer prices rose steeply after the West Asia crisis. Management said modal prices for dielectric films are now above INR550/kg, with prices moving up almost every alternate week, but it would not give exact current prices.
The company held prices lower earlier to anticipate new capacity; price increases are now being pursued, reflecting replacement cost of polymers.
Imports mainly from China and Korea (commodity grades) and Europe (high-value grades); management sees limited threat from imports given indigenous supply and faster delivery.
Customers are existing capacitor manufacturers; validation of ultrathin films can take zero to many months depending on customer and application.

590073|2026-09.headline: Wheels India Q2 FY27 standalone revenue rose 36% to INR1,598 crores and net profit to INR53.4 crores, with EBITDA margin at about 8%.
590073|2026-09.overview: Standalone revenue grew 36% YoY to INR1,598 crores from INR1,179 crores, and net profit rose to INR53.4 crores from INR27.8 crores. Growth came mainly from earthmover wheels (largely exported), air suspension and the domestic auto segment, while the industrial segment grew more slowly. EBITDA was about 8% and PBT about 4%, and management said the debt repayment done in the last days of the quarter meant no interest benefit was captured yet. Management flagged inflation, a high GST 2.0 base from H2 FY26 that may slow growth from Q3, and a weak monsoon affecting tractor demand in some states.

segments.name: Auto (car, truck, tractor, earthmover wheels, air suspension)
segments.commentary: Grew almost 40% YoY, driven mainly by earthmover wheels and air suspension, with regular wheels also contributing. Air suspension volume grew about 50% YoY.

segments.name: Industrial (windmill, hydraulics, construction fabrication, machining)
segments.commentary: Growth was muted. Construction fabrication was slow, and windmill was seasonally slow with recovery expected from Q3. Management guided for industrial to turn profitable by Q3-Q4.

segments.name: Cast aluminium (LPDC) wheels
segments.commentary: Capacity is 80,000 wheels/month, rising to 130,000 by end-March 2027. Breakeven of about 40,000/month reached, with PBT positive expected from December. Management targets 10-15% share of passenger car aluminium wheels within about a year.

segments.name: Windmill machining
segments.commentary: Job-work business with a double-digit EBITDA margin, roughly INR10 crores/month, expected to roughly double over two years as the casting partner scales from 3,500 to 5,000 tonnes/month.

segments.name: Hydraulic cylinders
segments.commentary: Low single-digit margin today. Scale-up expected from Q4 FY27 after layout changes, with supplies to international partners planned from January.

guidance_outlook: Double-digit EBITDA margin targeted in about two years; management said it would reach 10-12% EBITDA at 100,000 aluminium wheels/month, expected around Q1 FY28.
Price pass-through claims for raw materials and fuel (West Asia crisis) are in progress; closure expected by Q3, with margin upside from Q3 as management described it.
Capex guided at INR400-450 crores for FY27: about INR200 crores for aluminium wheels, about INR100 crores for industrial, and INR100-150 crores for conventional steel wheels.
Growth expected to slow from Q3 FY27 due to the high GST 2.0 base; visibility beyond Q3 is limited, per management.
Working capital is not expected to rise further at current activity levels, so accruals over the next two quarters will fund capex; undrawn loan lines remain available.
capex_capacity: Cast aluminium wheels: capacity 80,000/month now, 130,000/month by end-March 2027, with a 170,000 phase also referenced; roughly INR200 crores for adding about 90,000/month at an existing site. Next-phase capex already being planned.
Air suspension volumes growing about 50% YoY; management plans further capacity additions at its own and supplier facilities.
Hydraulic cylinders: layout changes under way, output step-up from January.
Windmill machining: casting partner expanding from 3,500 to 5,000 tonnes/month from December-January, with a further step to 6,500 tonnes/month in 12-18 months.
Bosch JV (electronic air suspension for commercial vehicles, about INR100 crores investment, Wheels India 20% stake) awaiting European competition clearance.
demand_pricing: Management described demand as strong across segments, but expects growth to slow from Q3 due to the GST 2.0 base effect and flagged inflation concerns.
Tractor demand grew strongly in H1, but poor monsoon in Maharashtra, Rajasthan, Karnataka and Andhra Pradesh may moderate it from Q4; north India remains firm. Globally the tractor cycle is down.
Aluminium wheel economics: average realisation about INR5,000/wheel; management said breakeven is about 40,000/month.
Passenger car steel wheels: about 35% share (management says the 40% aluminium segment is included in that base). Aluminium wheel share is in the low single digits, with a 10-15% target.
US business grew 50% in H1, driven by earthmover and windmill products. Management said order visibility is monthly customer schedules, not a formal order book.
Management said it will not enter truck air suspension, which it views as low margin (below double-digit EBITDA).

qa_highlights.question: What is the path to double-digit EBITDA margins, and what growth is reasonable over 1-2 years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management targets double-digit EBITDA from about two years out, driven by scaling subscale businesses (aluminium wheels, hydraulics, tractor components, air suspension). Air suspension and aluminium wheels are the near-term volume drivers.

qa_highlights.question: Where are we on raw-material and fuel price pass-through?
qa_highlights.answer: RM pass-through is automatic with about a one-quarter lag. Fuel-related claims are being settled with customers, with closure expected by Q3, so no major Q2/Q3 impact is expected.

qa_highlights.question: When will aluminium wheels reach EBITDA and PBT breakeven?
qa_highlights.answer: Already EBITDA positive and at about 40,000/month breakeven. Excess older stock held back during the West Asia crisis is still landing, and PBT positive is expected from December.

qa_highlights.question: What capex is needed per 1 lakh aluminium wheels, and what asset turnover?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR200 crores for roughly 90,000 wheels/month at an existing site. Asset turnover assumed at about INR5,000 per wheel x 90,000 x 12 per year.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the industrial segment so low-margin, and what is the capex split?
qa_highlights.answer: Of INR400-450 crores FY27 capex, about INR100 crores is industrial. Windmill is double-digit margin, hydraulics low single-digit with a Q4 scale-up, and construction fabrication recovering after monsoon. Industrial is expected to reach double-digit margin in 3-4 quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Why is H1 operating cash flow negative, and will cash repay debt?
qa_highlights.answer: September sales spike raised receivables and inventory, plus about INR90 crores of Q2 capex. About INR282 crores of bill discounting and INR142 crores of WCDL were repaid from issue proceeds. Future accruals over two quarters will fund capex, not working capital.

qa_highlights.question: What are export guidance and the split between auto and industrial exports?
qa_highlights.answer: H1 exports about INR760 crores; management said full-year exports could roughly double on that base, but no formal guidance was given. Stronger export growth is expected next calendar year, with the US up 50%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the GST refund blockage and is there a provision?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR130-140 crores of inverted-duty GST credit is stuck on the portal. Refunds are being collected via exports and inverted duty routes; no provision required, as it is a timing delay.

risks_watch: Growth slowdown from Q3 FY27 due to high GST 2.0 base and inflation; tractor demand weakness from poor monsoon in several states.
Aluminium wheel ramp-up execution: 130,000/month by March 2027 and PBT positive from December depend on clearing older stock and volume ramp-up.
Negative H1 operating cash flow and about INR130-140 crores of GST credit stuck in the portal, which delays cash.
Tariff and duty volatility on US exports; management said duties keep changing and refunds are delayed.
Industrial segment margin (about 3%) must recover to meet targets; hydraulics and fabrication timelines are back-end loaded to Q3-Q4.
